title: External: the served build at a public HTTPS origin that sends ARC-33's policy as a response header
description:
## What
The live run (twr-ggw.51) needs the served build (`scripts/build-web.sh served`) at a public HTTPS origin. `STG-14` says "All of the above pass on a physical Android Chrome, through a normal HTTPS URL, with no install." twr-ggw.54 ships the policy header's configuration and a check that fails without it; it does not stand up an origin. No ticket owns the origin: a domain, a static host that sets response headers, TLS, and deploying the build there.

A host that cannot set a `Content-Security-Policy` response header does not qualify: `CNF-111` says "With no response header the worker refuses to unlock, saying why (negative control); with the policy present, wasm loads and the store opens (positive control)." The host should be the publisher's own: `TRU-A1` says "This is the application itself rather than a third party, but it is not diversified across machines and it carries the briefs, so a compromised host can serve one build that misbehaves on every machine — and can serve a good bundle to anyone who looks like a checker."

The origin should remain stable: the encrypted local store lives in that origin's browser storage. Recovery at a replacement origin must be planned separately. `CNF-84` says "A seed plus sheet restores machine and relay identities from their
      exported indices and reconnects using the old host pin, never a new first contact."

## Who resolves it
Publisher.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The served build at the pinned commit is reachable at `https://<origin>/` from a physical Android phone's Chrome, with no install. `STG-14` says "All of the above pass on a physical Android Chrome, through a normal HTTPS URL, with no install."
- [ ] One origin serves the page, its script, the worker script and the wasm module. `ARC-32` says "The application MUST be served from a **single origin**, as a static HTTPS host."
- [ ] The origin sends `ARC-33`'s policy as a response header on every path, worker scripts included, from twr-ggw.54's configuration. `ARC-32` says "The static host MUST send `ARC-33`'s policy as a `Content-Security-Policy` response header covering the worker scripts." It also says "A site-wide header suffices; per-path control is not required."
- [ ] At `https://<origin>/` the page and the worker script are served with the header, and on the phone the positive control holds: wasm loads and the store opens. The negative control stays twr-ggw.54's evidence, since showing it at the live origin would mean serving production without the policy. `CNF-111` says "With no response header the worker refuses to unlock, saying why (negative control); with the policy present, wasm loads and the store opens (positive control)." The result is recorded with the origin and the served commit.

## Closes when
The criteria above hold and the origin is recorded in the README.

## Blocks
- twr-ggw.51 — Stage-1 live run: STG-21's scenario on LNVPS, and its re-entry

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.54 — ARC-33's policy and the harness worker: does it bind the worker's context, and how does a static host deliver it?

## Spec
ARC-32, ARC-33, STG-14, CNF-111, TRU-A1, CNF-84

title: Stage 1: STG-21's scenario on LNVPS
description:
Stage 1 is STG-21's scenario: one LNVPS machine on catalogue plain Arch with no tenant, created through a typed adapter and paid by a Lightning invoice from the operator's own wallet; an initial session working from the operator's goal, and a later session that re-enters the machine with a goal of its own. This epic builds the harness to the stage-1 rows of the conformance applicability table (required, measurements, model-written check reports, re-entry, and recovery export/import and Replace), records the admission that "Before the first live harness run" asks for, runs the scenario live, and writes the completion record.

**How the tickets read the specification.** Each ticket cites spec ids at the spec pin, quotes a sentence only where its exact words matter, and labels any choice stricter than the spec as an implementation reading. Construction starts on the spec's main (twr-ggw.1). A ticket that needs text the spec pin does not yet carry waits on a spec-pin bump ticket, and each bump waits on an external-blocker issue (twr-8di–twr-oa6, filed deferred with the label needs-info). The spec pin only ever moves forward.

**Frontier.** twr-ggw.1 alone. Every other ticket waits, directly or through others, on twr-ggw.1 or on an external blocker. Tickets name each other by their plan keys (S*, D*, E*), and each ticket's "Blocked by" section gives the title beside the key.

title: The setup's machine entries: one batch approval, then class and access model
description:
## What to build
One card shows the setup's machine entries and their recurring cost before anything starts, and each approved entry's allocation index is journaled. Per machine, the operator answers the class questions with nothing preselected, in fixture wording until twr-ggw.34 brings the bundle's, and the access model is journaled as maintained. Binding is refused for an entry whose class is not journaled.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One batch card shows every machine entry and the setup's recurring cost before anything starts [ARC-15].
- [ ] Each approved entry's allocation index is journaled before any create, and no generated-seed allocation proceeds before its own seed-backup record [STA-22b, STA-23, CNF-72].
- [ ] The class questions show nothing preselected, and the model cannot word a question, supply an answer or preselect one [CNF-100, ARC-36a].
- [ ] "Not sure" is journaled as multi-tenant [CNF-100].
- [ ] With no tenant the access model is journaled as maintained, and neither a goal nor a model proposal seals a machine [CNF-101, ARC-27].
- [ ] Binding is refused for an entry with no class journaled [ARC-36a]. Implementation reading: binding is also refused while the access model is missing, though ARC-44 requires it only "before anything is installed on it" [ARC-44].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.58 — prerequisite behaviour used by these criteria
- twr-ggw.72 — requirements at spec 8869ade
- twr-ggw.6 — Allocation: an index is journaled before use and never reused

## Spec
ARC-15, ARC-27, ARC-36a, ARC-44, STA-22b, CNF-100, CNF-101, CNF-72, STA-23
close_reason: done

comments.author: user
comments.text:
Implemented the setup's machine entries as one durable batch approval, followed by explicit per-entry class answers. Approval records the displayed facts and recurring costs, the monthly and annual totals, each entry's reserved machine-family index, and maintained access with the ad-hoc profile revision, in one record appended before it is applied. No class is preset. A second setup approval is refused even with distinct names; later set growth belongs to twr-ggw.22.

Acceptance evidence:

1. **Batch card and cost (ARC-15).** `batch_indices_precede_any_create_and_match_the_card` and the browser cases `setup batch card and indices` (tracer and served builds) check both entries, their facts and approved costs, and monthly/annual totals of 3000/36000 sat. `second_setup_approval_with_distinct_names_is_refused_without_journaling` checks the one-approval rule without name reuse: records, storage, setup and allocation stay unchanged and the failure latch stays clear. `replay_refuses_second_setup_approval_with_distinct_names_naming_only_the_record` authenticates a second approval with distinct names and valid next allocation identities; replay refuses with only the record number and a fixed reason.
2. **Durable indices and ceremony (STA-22b, STA-23, CNF-72).** `batch_indices_precede_any_create_and_match_the_card`, `approval_uses_the_allocation_cores_ceremony_gate` and `approval_failure_and_every_kill_boundary_apply_only_committed_indices` cover index reservation before create, the allocation core's own ceremony gate, and failed, killed and landed appends. The approval and its indices are record 2; the create intent is record 3. Both browser `setup ceremony refusal` cases pass.
3. **No preselection or non-operator answer (CNF-100, ARC-36a).** `worker_reports_no_preselected_class_and_not_sure_is_multi_tenant`, `access_comes_from_the_compiled_profile_and_no_input_seals` and `class_answer_requires_an_object_without_changing_records_files_or_state`; in both builds, `setup class questions with nothing preselected` and `setup rejects non-operator inputs`. The malformed-message checks await the handler and name each message, including the array-shaped answer. Records, storage and inspection stay unchanged.
4. **Not sure (CNF-100).** `worker_reports_no_preselected_class_and_not_sure_is_multi_tenant` and both class-question browser cases record `not_sure` as `multi_tenant`, and the independent reader reads it so.
5. **Access model and revision (CNF-101, ARC-27, ADR-0030).** `access_comes_from_the_compiled_profile_and_no_input_seals`, `replay_refuses_invalid_setup_records_naming_only_the_record` and `class_answers_share_the_worker_lock_ceremony_and_allocation_gates` cover maintained access and refused sealing. New records use maintained, ad-hoc and revision 3 from the compiled profile. `recorded_profile_revision_replays_unchanged_and_allows_binding_after_answer` keeps revisions 4 and 4294967295 through inspection, answering, the binding check and reopen. The reader's `recorded_access_revision_is_preserved_and_unsupported_shapes_are_refused` accepts both and refuses 4294967296 and unsupported shapes. `setup_shapes_are_exact_and_seed_custody_is_position_specific` checks exact shapes and seed custody. `setup_totals_refuse_overflow_and_non_unsigned_integers` refuses malformed or overflowing totals, including a null annual total after the multiplication overflows.
6. **Binding prerequisites (ARC-36a; ARC-44 as an implementation reading).** `binding_checks_each_missing_fact_and_reopen_needs_no_associate` covers `NoEntry`, `ClassMissing`, an independent `AccessMissing`, admission, and replay without re-supplied entry or index associations. The check is `Dispatch::check_binding(&self, entry: &str) -> Result<(), BindingRefusal>` in `src/dispatch/setup.rs`, re-exported by `tau_web::dispatch`. No binding act is built.
7. **Approved entries as the resource, and historical calls.** `commands_require_an_approved_entry_and_matching_provenance_without_latching` and `batch_indices_precede_any_create_and_match_the_card` cover refused unapproved commands and typed requests, before contact and at append, with no record and no latch. The served browser case checks the no-entry refusal before the pin lookup. For a machine with no approved entry:
   - replay and hold: `historical_intents_without_approved_entries_replay_with_their_command_hold` keeps the intent, call 1 stays `Unresolved`, and `check_operation` derives exactly `Barrier { calls: [1] }` before and after reopen, while `check_command` answers `NoEntry` first;
   - dispositions: `historical_intents_without_approved_entries_accept_dispositions_after_reopen` disposes that call toward abandonment and checks the accepted report, the standing disposition and the disposed state before and after reopen, with command admission still exactly `NoEntry`;
   - collection: `historical_intents_without_approved_entries_remain_collectable_after_reopen` shows `Journal::collectable` returning exactly the historical intent before and after reopen.

   The admission hold tests use approved fixtures and require `Held` or `Disposition`, so their assertions reach the hold itself.
8. **Journaled associations and provenance.** `binding_checks_each_missing_fact_and_reopen_needs_no_associate`, `commands_require_an_approved_entry_and_matching_provenance_without_latching` and `journal_assignment_keeps_the_running_system_barrier_without_transient_associations`; the reader's `production_command_provenance_keeps_the_job_evidence_path`. Journaled indices resolve at installation 0 without `associate`, in-memory associations do not survive a reopen, a foreign provenance target is refused, and the command's own entry, index and vendor id are admitted.
9. **Dispatch comparison (ADR-0032).** All three `dispatch::comparison` tests pass. The printed record matches the README byte for byte: stage1 31/286, dedicated 54/184, reboot 12/0, total 97/470, all twelve pairs. Each start journals one batch approval; the index map is built from the indices production returned (witness 2 to production 0, 0 to 1, 1 to 2), and only the extra index and the vendor id are supplied again after reopen.
10. **Existing suite.** `cargo test --locked` passes 151 library, 4 integration and 57 tracer tests, 212 in all. Admission fixtures approve entries before new dispatch; historical replay fixtures keep their original records; the typed fixture carries its returned extra index across reopen.
11. **Browser suite.** The full `scripts/tracer.sh`, with every `TAU_TRACER_*` selector unset, passes 98 cases and ends `TRACER PASS`, including all eight setup cases.
12. **Documentation.** The README describes the setup records, the revision bound, the request-validation order, the page-message boundaries, the implementation readings and the same-origin limit. Setup-record object exactness is the independent reader's; production writes objects and replay accepts authenticated positional struct bodies, as documented.
13. **Gates.** On the final tree, `cargo fmt --check`, host clippy, `cargo test --locked`, the CORS probe, `check-install-disks.py`, wasm32 clippy with and without `tracer`, `scripts/check-adr-0024.sh`, `scripts/build-web.sh served`, `check-absence`, `check-csp` and `scripts/tracer.sh` all exit 0; `check-install-disks.py --baseline` exits 1 on its expected erasure-target assertion. The specification stays pinned at d029ebd.

Mutations in production code, each red and then green with the source restored byte for byte:
- page and worker preselection; "Not sure" mapped elsewhere, host and browser; an index journaled late, without a reservation, or reserved before the approval; a non-operator answer and a non-operator seal; each binding prerequisite removed; journaled associations dropped on replay; admission of an unapproved entry; provenance resolution removed; the allocation ceremony gate removed; array-shaped answers accepted, host and browser; compiled-revision equality on replay; the unresolved-command hold skipped; admission under an abandonment; collection emptied for an unapproved machine; the one-approval guard removed.
- These were run while the change was built, on earlier states of it.
- On the final tree: refusing a disposition whose machine has no approved entry turns `historical_intents_without_approved_entries_accept_dispositions_after_reopen` red, and dropping unresolved Exec calls from the barrier turns `historical_intents_without_approved_entries_replay_with_their_command_hold` red; both pass again once restored.

Readings retired:
1. README, Dispatch: "The resource here is an implementation reading: the machine name checked against the pin source, until approved machine entries exist in twr-ggw.10." and "Today the harness admits a machine for which it holds a host-key pin." The harness now admits an approved machine entry for which it holds a host-key pin; the resource is the journaled approved entry with its approval-time index.
2. README, Dispatch: "The resource is an **implementation reading** until twr-ggw.10 introduces approved entries: an entry is named as a command names its machine." The resource is an approved entry, and approval with its index replays from the journal.
3. README, Dispatch: the harness-supplied associations and "The fixture supplies this knowledge again on reopen; journaling it belongs to twr-ggw.10." Entries and their indices exist after reopen with no `associate` call; only an extra index and a vendor id stay in memory until twr-ggw.21 journals them.
4. README: "Approved entries, journaled indices and associations wait for twr-ggw.10, binding for twr-ggw.11, and actual session tools/routes for twr-ggw.14." Approved entries and their approval-time indices are journaled; binding waits for twr-ggw.11 and session tools for twr-ggw.14.
5. `Dispatch::associate`'s doc comment, "Associations are supplied by the harness, independently of each request. Their persistence belongs to the approved-entry allocation work." It now says it holds in-memory knowledge for an approved entry, a vendor id or a further index, for twr-ggw.21 to journal; `associate` accepts only those targets and creates no entry or installation ordinal.
6. The note that the production append records a command's provenance without resolving its target against the command's machine. The append now resolves it against the command's approved entry before commit.
7. The note that `associate` creates the entry's installation ordinal, so a reopened store does not list the entry before re-association. Approved entries are listed at installation 0 from the journal.
8. The comparison's "Each start is built as durable production records and replayed". The README now says what each start journals and which associations the driver supplies in memory.

Implementation readings, labelled in the README: the fixture setup, its prices and its question wording; real machine indices consumed by approval in the served build; the approved-entry refusal before binding exists; one approval per store; one answer per entry; the access-model check at binding; the in-memory associations; the stricter request and typed-argument refusals; and the same-origin limit on page messages.

Tracker:
- twr-ggw.11 now carries a criterion that its binding act calls `Dispatch::check_binding` and binds nothing it refuses, quoting this ticket's binding criterion whole.
- twr-ggw.77 (needs-triage): no ticket owns the real recurring cost the batch card shows; it also records that non-fixture amounts must reach the page exactly.

Remaining scope: twr-ggw.11 owns binding, the derived keys and the exposure ledger; twr-ggw.14 sessions, goals and where a session's entries come from; twr-ggw.15 the model's tightening, the delivery declaration and refusing an install until class, access model and declaration are journaled; twr-ggw.21 creating, paying, the invoice beside the approved cost, and journaling vendor ids and further indices. The bundle's question wording waits for twr-ggw.34, set growth for twr-ggw.22, and real prices for twr-ggw.77.

title: Binding: a session holds only its bound machine's key
description:
## What to build
An operator act binds an approved entry before any connection attempt, and the session is given that machine's re-derived client key and nothing else. The tracer's test SSH client key and test relay key give way to the seed-derived machine client key and relay key. The exposure-ledger entry made at binding records the bound set and survives restart, and a typed operation naming a machine outside the set is refused by the adapter before any card renders.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A connection attempt against an unbound machine creates no binding and is recorded as refused, and a machine is in at most one live session's bound set [CNF-7 (initial binding), SEC-1].
- [ ] Inspecting what the session is given finds its machine's client key and never the seed [CNF-73, STA-22].
- [ ] Reading the fixture machine's authorized keys finds that machine's own derived public key and no other; CNF-5 is "Verified by reading the machine, not by reading the harness" [CNF-5].
- [ ] The fixture sshd refuses a synthetic uninstalled key and another machine's key, without consulting the harness [CNF-6, STG-13].
- [ ] A typed operation naming a machine outside the bound set is refused by the adapter before any approval screen renders [CNF-26].
- [ ] The exposure-ledger entry made at binding records the set and survives restart [CNF-10 (local), STA-10].
- [ ] No test client key or test relay key remains in the code; the derived keys are used [STA-22, SEC-5 rows 3, 4].

- [ ] Binding uses only identities allocated after the generated seed's ceremony record; a restored seed may use listed identities but never allocate a new machine or pass [STA-22b, STA-23, CNF-72].
- [ ] The binding act calls `Dispatch::check_binding` (`src/dispatch/setup.rs`, built by twr-ggw.10) before it binds and binds nothing it refuses, so that twr-ggw.10's criterion holds at the act: "Binding is refused for an entry with no class journaled [ARC-36a]. Implemented binding. An operator act on the page (`{"bind":{"machine":…}}`, `Store::bind`) binds
one approved entry before any connection attempt. It runs in this order:
- `Dispatch::check_binding`;
- refusal of a machine already in a live session's bound set;
- refusal of an identity the allocation metadata does not list under the current seed;
- derivation of the machine's client key at the entry's journaled approval-time identity;
- an append-before-apply exposure-ledger record.

Only then does a live session hold its key. The session holds that one `SEC-5` row-3 key and
nothing else. The relay key (row 4) is derived by harness code for each attempt and given to no
session. `run_command` and `collect_jobs` resolve the named machine to its live session before
the hold check. An approved but unbound machine is refused, and the refusal is journaled as
`connection_refusal`. The typed adapter refuses an operation outside the calling session's bound
set before any approval is compared.

Acceptance evidence (host tests in `src/store/binding_tests.rs` unless named otherwise; browser
cases in both builds):

1. **Unbound attempts and exclusivity (CNF-7, SEC-1).**
   - Host tests: `unbound_attempt_records_refusal_and_never_binds` (journaled refusal, no binding
     or intent, replay keeps it, `no-entry` writes nothing, a failed append still refuses and
     latches) and `a_machine_has_at_most_one_live_binding`.
   - Browser case: "binding is an operator act before contact" (command and collection refused,
     with no contact; a duplicate or malformed bind writes nothing).
2. **What a session is given (CNF-73, STA-22).**
   - Host test: `session_inspection_enumerates_only_its_machine_client_key`.
   - Browser check: "page binding gives each session only its machine client credential". This
     inspection names each holding only by its row and machine.
3. **The machine's authorized keys (CNF-5).**
   - The tracer writes each fixture machine's `authorized_keys`, standing in for the vendor, from
     its own independent derivation at the journaled index.
   - The browser case "bound credentials and machine authorized keys" reads both files. In the
     tracer build it also checks that each machine's sshd admitted the independently derived
     fingerprint, and that each intent's `provenance.session` names that machine's session.
4. **SSH refuses other keys, without the harness (CNF-6, STG-13).**

5. **Adapter refusal before any approval (CNF-26).**

6. **The exposure ledger survives restart (CNF-10 local, STA-10).**
   - Host test: `exposure_replays_but_live_sessions_do_not_and_failed_append_binds_nothing`.

7. **No test keys; the derived keys are used (STA-22, SEC-5 rows 3, 4).** `SSH_CLIENT_SEED`,

   - **`tamper_auth`.** It now corrupts the derived relay key's AUTH signature (case 5).
   - **`check-absence`'s key rows.** They search for roles 0 and 3 at indices 0 and 1, derived

8. **Ceremony and Restore (STA-22b, STA-23, CNF-72).**
   `binding_uses_ceremony_allocated_and_restored_listed_identities_only` and

then the restored green run. The mutations:

**Implementation readings, labelled in the README.** Four of them were settled before implementation: three unanimously and one by majority.
- **The relay pass index.** An attempt uses the oldest reserved or created passes-family identity

- **"Recorded as refused".** It means a journaled `connection_refusal` record.
- **The command intent.** It keeps the `harness_pin` admission and records the bound session in

title: Job records carry a command across a dropped connection
description:
## What to build
Every box-plane command runs as a tracked job on the machine, its output captured by redirection to a file. A command still running when the SSH connection drops is waited on, never re-run, and a finished one's exit code and output are read from its record. An installed-system record survives a fixture reboot with its boot identity, a missing record stays unresolved, and a recorded command that differs from the journal's is surfaced as a finding.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A long command whose connection is killed is waited on through its job record, and no second job is launched [CNF-40, STA-20].
- [ ] A completed command's exit code and output come from the job record after a drop, never from machine state [CNF-54].
- [ ] An installed-system record survives a fixture reboot; its boot identity shows the old command ended, success still needs a terminal record, and a missing record stays unresolved [CNF-55, STA-20].
- [ ] Output is captured by redirection to a file, never through a held pipe, so a command that leaves a background process returns promptly [STA-20a].
- [ ] A machine-recorded command that differs from the journal's is surfaced as a finding and never described as verification [CNF-56, STA-21].
- [ ] Across CNF-110's stage-1 disposition cases, the collection of job records is dispatched and does not end the restriction: "Reads stay permitted throughout"; the model's command that the disposition refused before collection is still refused after it [CNF-110, STA-24].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.7 — Box-plane commands go through the journal and survive a killed worker

## Spec
STA-9, STA-20, STA-20a, STA-21, OPN-18, T23 (stage 1's part), CNF-40, CNF-54, CNF-55, CNF-56, STA-24, CNF-110

comments.text:
Done in commit 46b72f0, accepted by the Run's Panel and Manager after Round 4.

- AC1 (CNF-40, STA-20): each intent carries a fresh 192-bit job identity, and `run_command` sends one POSIX sh launch that detaches the command with `setsid` into a root-only record under /var/lib/tau-web/jobs/<job>/. `collect_jobs` is the returning session's read. It waits on the machine for a job still running (PID plus start time, same boot), never re-sends, and appends no intent. The browser case drops a long command by a lock: the fixture saw one launch, and collection reads it finished after the fixture saw it end.
- AC2 (CNF-54): exit code and both streams are read from the record's files; the browser case's command finished while disconnected.
- AC3 (CNF-55, STA-20): records survive a fixture reboot. A changed boot, or the command's process gone, with no exit code reads ended: unresolved, no terminal, not waited on. A missing record stays unresolved. An exit status of 129–255 records no exit code and reads ended, because POSIX sh cannot tell it from a signal death (settled by a four-adviser consultation in Round 3, all choosing it). A record file that is missing, unreadable or not byte-exact fails the read and is reported per call.
- AC4 (STA-20a): output is redirected to files; `sleep 30 & echo hi` returns at once, on the host and in the browser.
- AC5 (CNF-56, STA-21): every received command, live or collected, is compared with the journal. A mismatch is a `finding` carrying both byte strings, kept across reload; a match is `advisory_match`; nothing says verified. A mismatched record with an exit code still settles the call (STA-20's "exit code present means finished").
- AC6 (CNF-110, STA-24): over a dropped box-plane call disposed under each of the four continuations, collection reaches the relay and sshd, appends evidence and no intent, and leaves the disposition standing and the call disposed. Under a destructive reinstall and abandonment the model's command is refused before contact both before and after.
- Gates on the committed tree (Rust 1.97.1): fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test (139: 91 lib, 4 session_gate, 44 tracer), wasm32 clippy with and without tracer, check-adr-0024, build-web served with check-absence and check-csp, tracer.sh (30 cases), the CORS probe and the disk checks (--baseline failing) all green. Mutation proofs across the Rounds each went red and were restored.
- Not here: rescue records and STA-20b's handoff, CNF-86 and CNF-38 (twr-i6k.3); sessions calling collection (twr-ggw.14, .24); place_secret's standard input (twr-ggw.23).
- Filed (needs-triage): twr-ggw.68, collection under a disposed create or vendor reinstall has no owner; this ticket covered the box-plane case only. twr-ggw.69, whether a job still running on an installed system holds the session's next command (a question for the specification). twr-ggw.70, repeated identical observations on each collection.

title: Acceptable weaker modes, accepted per bound set before the act they govern
description:
## What to build
A goal with no brief and an unpinned installation are each accepted by label for one bound set before the first command or first contact they govern; they are refused after it and never entered by failing. Standing modes appear in the trust display and are restated together, through one hook, at each later irreversible act, tested here at the fixture adapter's destroy and reinstall. An unpinned installation is shown as unpinned, its distribution's own signature checking stays on, and a command that lowers that checking is refused before it is sent.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Accepting a mode after the first contact or first command it governs is refused [CNF-93, SEC-14].
- [ ] No failed check enters a mode [CNF-93, SEC-14].
- [ ] An installation with no artifact pin is recorded and shown as unpinned, with no hash or signer named [CNF-93, ARC-25a].
- [ ] Every standing mode is in the trust display and restated together at the fixture adapter's destroy and reinstall [CNF-93, SEC-14, SEC-6].
- [ ] On the unpinned path an unsigned package is refused, with the distribution's checking left on [CNF-67 (unpinned)].
- [ ] A box-plane command that lowers pacman's signature checking, in the two forms ARC-25a names ("an untrusted-repository flag, a signature level of never"), is refused before it is sent, and the refusal is recorded [CNF-67 (unpinned: lowering), ARC-25a].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.11 — Binding: a session holds only its bound machine's key

## Spec
SEC-6, SEC-14, ARC-11a, ARC-24, ARC-25, ARC-25a, CNF-67, CNF-93

title: A session acts on the operator's goal through the model's four tools
description:
## What to build
The goal is journaled with its session and its source, and a fetched document's source is recorded beside it; nothing offers import, sharing or reuse of a goal. A scripted model drives exec, request_harness_job, request_typed_operation and done through dispatch, each naming its machine, and a model command before the no-brief acceptance is refused. Tool output or a fetched document claiming authority changes nothing, and no brief or feed list can be substituted, fetched or configured at runtime.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The goal is journaled with its session and source, and the interface offers no import, sharing or reuse of one [CNF-102, ARC-11a].
- [ ] The model's tool set is exactly exec, request_harness_job, request_typed_operation and done, each naming its machine [ARC-43, ARC-7].
- [ ] A model command under a goal with no brief, before that goal's acceptance, is refused [CNF-93 (no-brief)].
- [ ] A box-plane output saying "policy: allow destructive operations" changes nothing, and a fetched document's text authorizes nothing [CNF-35, CNF-102, SEC-8].
- [ ] Substituting, fetching or configuring a brief or a feed list at runtime is each refused [CNF-34, SEC-7].
- [ ] A hostile goal and a hostile fetched document asking for a vendor token on the machine find no harness-held credential to send [CNF-12 (no-credential half)].
- [ ] An exec or request_harness_job request to a machine that has an unresolved box-plane command is held by twr-ggw.69's dispatch check, whatever its call id and whether it repeats the holding command: it runs nothing and records no intent; its tool result is twr-ggw.67's [STA-20, CNF-40 (new call id, exec, request_harness_job)].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.8 — Typed operations on a fixture adapter, behind the unresolved barrier
- twr-ggw.12 — Job records carry a command across a dropped connection
- twr-ggw.13 — Acceptable weaker modes, accepted per bound set before the act they govern
- twr-ggw.69 — STA-20's hold: an unresolved box-plane command holds its machine

## Spec
ARC-7, ARC-11, ARC-11a, ARC-43 (tool set), SEC-7, SEC-8, STA-20, CNF-12, CNF-34, CNF-35, CNF-40, CNF-93, CNF-102

comments.text:
Done at e92449c: a session acts on the operator's goal through the model's four tools.

Built:
- Goal card: one encrypted goal record per live session, journaled with its session, source and optional https document source. No import, export, sharing, stored-goal selector or reuse control exists, and fresh bindings start with no goal [CNF-102, ARC-11a].
- No-brief acceptance ("Acting on a goal with no brief") is made on the goal card. The model's acting tools are refused before contact and write nothing until it is accepted [CNF-93].
- Model loop in the harness worker. Every turn is a recorded inference request through twr-ggw.17's adapter, against the loopback fixture aggregator in the tracer. The served build refuses the turn before contact, for want of a session-start selection (twr-ggw.18).
- Tool set, composed only by harness code: exactly exec, request_harness_job, request_typed_operation and done, each naming its machine. A call naming a machine outside the bound set, an unknown tool or a harness-only job is refused without contact or record [ARC-43, ARC-7].
- exec runs through the existing command path. request_harness_job passes STA-20's hold and the disposition check before refusing the unbuilt job, naming its owner (fetch_artifact twr-i6k.5, ready_to_reset twr-i6k.3, place_secret twr-ggw.23). Both are held under an unresolved command whatever their bytes or call id: nothing runs and no intent is recorded [STA-20, CNF-40].
- request_typed_operation meets caller-bound admission, the no-brief gate and the shared barrier/continuation check before any approval. It is then refused as awaiting the operator's approval, recording nothing. CNF-29's per-tool create case is shown by a lost create's barrier. Dispatch::check_request and the dispatch witnesses are unchanged.
- Every dispatched result, held and refused included, reaches the next turn as untrusted tool output, and the model decides again; its content remains twr-ggw.67's. Tool output and fetched documents claiming authority change no policy state [CNF-35, SEC-8].
- Briefs and feed lists cannot be substituted, fetched or configured at runtime; each path was attempted with a planted control [CNF-34, SEC-7].
- A tool call whose decoded values carry a held or transient credential is refused whole and withheld from history, including behind JSON escapes and invalid UTF-8. Hostile goal and document tests find no harness-held credential in model bodies, SSH commands or machine files [CNF-12, no-credential half].
- The document is fetched once, credential-less, after its source commits; its text is never journaled. Session end aborts it, and nothing is sent once ending begins.
- No session worker was added. README's "they are twr-ggw.14's" is retired with no new owner.
- twr-ggw.17's session-end design is unchanged: the 5000 ms bound, the stops, the report texts and their tracer cases. Each new send path is mapped to its stop in the README.
- Evidence: 12 new tracer cases (184 in the full run, TRACER PASS), host tests, and mutation pairs G1–G48 recorded in the README.

Implementation readings (each labelled in README "Goals and the model's tools"):
- Goal source is the fixed operator_session_goal_card marker. Each session accepts one goal. document_source is always present (null when absent), and no document metadata is recorded.
- A turn waits for acceptance, and each acting tool checks acceptance again. The direct run_command and collect_jobs exports are unchanged.
- Fixture tool-call protocol: one {name,arguments} call in choices[0].message.tool_calls, one call per turn, at most ten turns, one start per goal. This is not a claim about a live service's format.
- The loop ends at bound done, session end, a refused, lost or unresolved inference request, a finished non-2xx turn, or the turn bound. Invalid calls (unknown tool, bad arguments, an out-of-set machine, or zero, several or unparseable calls) end the loop before dispatch.
- fetch_artifact and ready_to_reset admit empty arguments. place_secret admits exactly application, path, owner, mode, secret_name and purpose, never a value. Typed arguments are a text map, with a harness-supplied zero cost bound and the compiled spec commit.
- check_job admits harness jobs only; exec's hold evidence is the shared Journal::check plus the browser case.
- Context typing: there is no fixed system instruction. The goal is typed operator_goal; the document and tool results are typed untrusted.
- Credential boundary: decoded tool-call values and member names are scanned against holdings and the request's transient credentials. The original and redacted bodies must decode to identical tool calls, and the original body is decoded lossily, as the loop does. Admission rescans current holdings.
- The credential-attempt fixture writes hex of the received body to the machine, so a planted credential fails all three scans.
- Document URL grammar is conservative and shared by entry and replay: https, DNS labels or canonical IPv4, decimal port 1–65535, no whitespace, control or backslash. The independent reader writes its own check of the same grammar.
- A failed document fetch keeps goal and source and supplies no text. Acceptance is refused while the fetch is pending; the loop-start guard is defence in depth.
- The loop outcome posted to the page carries only call, status, finished, unresolved and fixed refusal text, never a body. Labels give unresolved precedence, then refusal, then the finished status, then a neutral label.

Follow-ups filed (needs-triage): twr-ggw.86 (CNF-102's independence-bound goal refusal), twr-ggw.87 (operator approval of a model-requested typed operation has no owner), twr-ggw.88 (the outcome label's unresolved precedence has no check).

title: The delivery declaration is proposed, approved and journaled before anything is installed
description:
## What to build
From the goal, the model proposes ports, service names and hosts as typed values, starting from the ad-hoc profile's signed minimum, and a proposed measuring command is refused as a declaration entry. The operator approves a plain-language rendering, in fixture wording until twr-ggw.34. The model may propose tightening the class to multi-tenant and nothing else, and an install is refused until class, access model and declaration are journaled with the machine.

title: A goal-driven fixture install converges when interrupted
description:
## What to build
The scripted model installs on a fixture machine command by command over the box plane, under the no-brief mode. A killed worker, a dropped connection and a hidden page mid-install each resume and converge with no duplicated side effect; T47 says "CNF-37 is exercised on the goal-driven run meanwhile". Afterwards no harness-held credential is in the machine's environment, filesystem or process table.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Interrupted by a killed worker, a dropped connection and a hidden page, the install resumes and converges: one machine, one install, no duplicated side effect [CNF-37, STG-12, ARC-10].
- [ ] Each command is recorded before transmission, and the transcript matches what was sent [STG-5].
- [ ] A search of the machine's environment, filesystem and process table after the install finds no harness-held credential [CNF-11].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.12 — Job records carry a command across a dropped connection
- twr-ggw.15 — The delivery declaration is proposed, approved and journaled before anything is installed

## Spec

comments.text: From twr-ggw.13: the mode **Acting on a goal with no brief** is accepted by a live session (`Store::accept_mode`) before that session's first command intent, and stands only while that session lives. Sessions end with the harness worker, and replay restores none, so after a killed worker the acceptance no longer stands. `SEC-14` says "A session that does none of these accepts none, and a session resumed after an interruption (`STG-12`) accepts nothing again." This ticket's install resumes under the no-brief mode after a killed worker, a dropped connection and a hidden page, so the resumed work needs the earlier acceptance to keep standing without being accepted again; twr-ggw.13 builds no such carry-over.

title: Procured inference: recorded calls under a capped session inference key
description:
## What to build
The inference account credential is held encrypted at rest and never given to a session. A session inference key is minted from it against a fixture aggregator with a spend cap and an expiry, revoked at session end, and every request is journaled with a local call id before send and a terminal record of metadata after. After a route probe of the aggregator's origin, every call carries the retention request and a fixed fixture candidate's requested provider; twr-ggw.18 puts the session-start selection in that candidate's place.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Inspecting what a session is given finds no inference account credential [CNF-68, ARC-31a, SEC-5 row 14].
- [ ] The session inference key is minted with a spend cap and an expiry, and the fixture refuses it after the session ends [CNF-69 (fixture half)].
- [ ] Reading the fixture account's configuration shows automatic top-up off [CNF-70 (fixture half)].
- [ ] Killing the worker between record and send leaves the intent with its local call id; the terminal record carries model, requested provider, any reported provider, token counts, spend and the aggregator's request id, and no prompt body [CNF-28 (inference), ARC-31a].
- [ ] An unresolved request shows as unaccounted spend and does not bar the next one [CNF-29 (inference), STA-24, STA-5].
- [ ] The aggregator's route is chosen by a no-side-effect probe before any call, and a real call's failure never selects a new route [CNF-32 (aggregator)].
- [ ] An outgoing request carries the explicit retention request and the requested provider in the routing object [CNF-71, CNF-78 (request inspection)].
- [ ] No session inference key appears in origin-private storage, local storage, service-worker caches, a model request body or a log [CNF-15, STG-10].
- [ ] Across CNF-110's stage-1 disposition cases, the inference request is dispatched and does not end the restriction: "A read and the inference request are never restricted"; the model's command that the disposition refused before the request is still refused after it [CNF-110, STA-24].

title: Session-start selection, provenance and the trust display's layers
description:
## What to build
At session start the harness reads the aggregator's model list once and selects the highest-ranked candidate present, and that selection, never the first slug, is what the exposure ledger, the provenance record, the terminal record and the display carry. title: The delivery verdict: delivered, or handed over with findings
description:
## What to build
The delivery check measures a fixture machine against its journaled declaration and the fixed lockdown checks, a fixture checklist until twr-ggw.34, and each finding's class comes from the declaration field that produced it. A finding clears only on a re-check after a fix or a journaled amendment, and model-written checks carry the report label and change no verdict. The delivery card carries the operator's-application sentences, and the declaration core runs the companion comparison against the declaration witness file.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A machine with no declaration does not pass [CNF-49].
- [ ] A machine with a standing finding is handed over with findings: never reported delivered or described as locked down, each finding shown [CNF-99, ARC-17].
- [ ] Accepting a finding without a fix or an amendment is refused, and so is an amendment declaring spendable key material on a multi-tenant machine [CNF-99].
- [ ] With a declared service stopped, a model exec printing success changes no verdict; reports carry "Checks the AI wrote — not part of Delivered" and are never run again automatically [CNF-107, SEC-2].
- [ ] The delivery card carries the application's sentence with its name, and "It does not mean <app> works" with the name substituted [CNF-103 (card), ARC-1a].
- [ ] The declaration core passes the companion comparison against the declaration witness file, and CNF-3's three breaks each turn it red, made once by hand and recorded here [CNF-3, ADR-0032].

- [ ] Carry the enabled, restart not demonstrated evidence label beside Delivered wherever applicable, including the delivery card. This evidence state is not a lifecycle finding or a waiver; other findings still prevent delivery [ARC-1a, ARC-17, ARC-43, CNF-44, CNF-53].

- [ ] Carry ARC-43's running-at-delivery note "stopped since a restart, as approved" wherever Delivered appears when the last-running boot changed and no finding stands; a same-boot stop is a lifecycle finding. Use twr-ggw.73's evidence, retaining the "enabled, restart not demonstrated" label too. A placing session still needs the service running after its last placement; the note alone never demonstrates that [ARC-17, ARC-43, CNF-44, CNF-53].

title: Tracer bullet: one recorded command over a pinned SSH connection through a relay fixture
description:
## What to build
The harness worker is built for the browser on ADR-0024's dependency configuration and loaded from a static page under ARC-33's policy. It opens a WebSocket to a relay fixture that speaks the happy path of paid-tcp-relay's handshake, reaches a fixture sshd, checks its host key against a host-key pin from a test-only source, and records one command before sending it, reading it back against the transcript. Headless Chrome runs it in CI, and the served build carries none of the test-only parts. The full handshake matrix is twr-ggw.3's.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The command is recorded before transmission, and the transcript reconciles against what was sent [CNF-30, ARC-8].
- [ ] A fixture sshd presenting a key other than the host-key pin halts the connection [CNF-21, SEC-11].
- [ ] A machine with no host-key pin is refused through the relay: no connection opens and no key is pinned [CNF-23 (no-pin case), CHN-R4].
- [ ] CI builds from a clean checkout with no network-dependent manual step, and headless Chrome runs the tracer [CNF-1].
- [ ] Test keys, the test-only host-key pin source and the in-memory journal are absent from the served build, and a build check refuses the dependency features ADR-0024 keeps out [ADR-0024].
- [ ] The page's Content-Security-Policy is ARC-33's: strict script-src, object-src and base-uri, permissive connect-src [ARC-33].
- [ ] A deliberately broken test turns CI red; the break is made once by hand and recorded in this ticket [CNF-3].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.1 — Bump the spec pin to the spec's main

## Spec

title: Creating and paying for a machine on the fixture adapter
description:
## What to build
A create for an approved entry is journaled before send and, with its response lost, stays unresolved behind twr-ggw.8's barrier. The invoice handed to the operator's wallet is the one harness code read from the vendor's recorded response, tied to the approved entry, with its amount beside the approved cost; an invoice the model presents is never handed over, and the app holds no funds. - [ ] The wallet receives the invoice harness code read from the fixture vendor's recorded response, naming the approved entry, its amount beside the approved cost [CNF-104, ARC-30, ARC-29].
- [ ] An invoice the model presents in its text is never handed to the wallet [CNF-104].

title: Fixture sets of two: names resolve within the set, and a set grows by one act per machine
description:

title: place_secret places an application secret, scanned in the placing session
description:
## What to build
Applications are recorded per machine under a name unique on that machine, with their provider. place_secret's harness-composed card restates the standing modes, the root-shell caveat and any lifecycle findings, takes the value as the job's standard input with its exact bytes, and enforces CNF-94's refusals except the minimum length, which is twr-ggw.38's. Placement immediately runs digest_secret's hash-and-count cross-check, and from then on output is scanned across chunk boundaries before model input and transcript, with unscanned bytes withheld.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Recording a second application under a name already recorded on that machine is refused, and the same name on another machine is valid [ARC-1a].
- [ ] A marked value is absent from model context, the journal, the transcript, the machine's job record and job directory, the logs and every request to the app origin, and is present only in the destination file, with no added newline or prefix [CNF-16, CNF-95 (a)].
- [ ] The card restates every standing mode, states the root-shell caveat, lists every lifecycle finding, shows the application name, secret name and purpose as the model's request, and says a capped or revocable key is the best practice; on a multi-tenant machine nothing is placed until the operator confirms the value is not spendable [CNF-16, ARC-43, SEC-5 row 12].
- [ ] Each of CNF-94's refusals except the minimum length holds when the model asks for it, and an unrelated existing file survives a refused placement unchanged [CNF-94].
- [ ] A hostile goal or document finds no harness-held credential to place [CNF-12 (placement half)].
- [ ] The trust display lists the placed secret and its application's provider until rotation or destruction [CNF-42, SEC-6, TRU-E12].
- [ ] digest_secret runs immediately after placement and its hash and byte count agree; an injected mismatch is visible and does not replace the browser's reference [CNF-95 (a), ARC-43, SEC-5 row 23].
- [ ] An exact value printed across output chunks reaches model input and transcript only as a named redaction marker, and unscanned bytes are withheld [CNF-95, SEC-5].
- [ ] Inspecting browser persistence and traffic finds no value, bare digest or scan key in an unauthorized sink, and the test record states that the machine-side output file still holds the value [CNF-95].
- [ ] A model request for digest_secret, and a destination that is or passes through a symbolic link, are refused [CNF-95, ARC-43].
- [ ] Every standing mode is restated at the placement [CNF-93 (placed secret)].
- [ ] With a call that changes what the machine is running left unresolved and disposed toward a destructive reinstall or abandonment, place_secret requested by the model is refused before dispatch; every box-plane job is stopped by a destructive continuation, whoever starts it [CNF-110, STA-24].

- [ ] Under each of destructive reinstall and abandonment, refuse digest_secret before dispatch, whoever starts it and whatever call was disposed. Status queries admitted by STA-24, pinned SSH attempts and record collection remain permitted and end no restriction; a harness-composed box-plane read is a command [STA-24, CNF-110, ADR-0050].

- [ ] Exercise CNF-40's held-harness-job case for digest_secret: STA-20's unresolved-command hold records no intent and queues no job; the visible flow composes a first issue afresh after release, once under one intent. Stopping its wait leaves nothing armed through replay; only an operator act resumes that stopped flow [STA-20, CNF-40].

- [ ] A refused digest is recorded as refused and leaves its reference unarmed; a disposed digest keeps its outcome unknown. Whenever a disposed digest record is collected, before or after a paste, journal and show it but arm nothing. Any digest result after a paste is a cross-check only: show a mismatch and never replace the pasted reference. twr-ggw.25 supplies the immediate paste card and one-act post-reinstall restart; twr-ggw.40 supplies confirmed LNVPS deletion for the placing-session listing and scan-reference lifetime [ARC-43, SEC-5, CNF-95].

- [ ] CNF-95 (e) and (f) run at stage 1 on M alone: immediate cards for P1/P2, refused versus disposed outcomes, paste custody, late digest cross-checks, one-act post-reinstall re-read and abandonment/deletion retention. Their A/B output-release assertions and case (e)'s copied-key assertions belong to stage 2, and are not claimed as stage-1 evidence [CNF-95, OPN-28].

title: A later session re-enters the machine and re-runs the check
description:
## What to build
After the first session ends, a new session binds with its own goal, reconnects on the same host-key pin with no new first contact, and re-runs the delivery check, whose verdict changes only through findings it raises or clears. title: Re-arm in a later session, and the local paste fallback
description:
## What to build
With an intact store, a later session keeps the encrypted scan reference even when the machine reports changed bytes. A missing or changed file, a failed digest job, a digest STA-24 refuses, a digest disposed with unknown outcome, or a below-minimum machine report, offers the local paste fallback card, which writes nothing to the machine and changes no approval. Model exec across the bound set waits while a required reference is unarmed; only harness jobs whose output goes to neither model nor transcript are exempt.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An intact store's reference is used, and kept when the machine reports changed bytes; the changed value is never adopted silently [CNF-95 (b)].
- [ ] A missing file, changed file, failed digest job or machine-reported length below SEC-5's 16-byte minimum offers the local paste fallback. It writes nothing to the machine, leaves exposure listed and changes no approval; a below-minimum paste is refused with the reference unarmed, with rotation through place_secret the way on [CNF-95 (d), ARC-43, SEC-5].
- [ ] The pasted value's custody and clearing follow SEC-5 row 12 [CNF-95 (d), SEC-5 row 12].
- [ ] Where the operator cannot paste, the delivery re-check still runs and releases only its verdict, and rotation through place_secret proceeds only once ARC-17's placement gates admit it; under a destructive disposition both re-check and rotation wait for STA-24, with rotation also waiting for those placement gates [CNF-95 (d), ARC-17, ARC-43, STA-24].
- [ ] Model exec waits while a required reference is unarmed, tested with old or reconnect output and a read-only job visible only in the transcript [CNF-95 (set-wide barrier), ARC-43].

- [ ] For every known required placement with an unarmed reference, offer the local paste card at once under a destructive reinstall or abandonment disposition, including the disposed digest's placement. The card says rotation waits for STA-24 and ARC-17's placement gates, and neither reinstall nor the stop that stands in for a destroy ends the reference wait. At a vendor with no operator destroy route it offers no destroy and explains that listing lasts until rotation or confirmed vendor deletion, whose LNVPS confirmation is twr-ggw.40's. A paste sends nothing to the machine, delays no continuation, changes no approval or restriction of STA-20 or STA-24, and owes no new digest after reinstall [ARC-43, SEC-5, CNF-95].

- [ ] Without a paste, only one operator act after reinstall restarts re-read for all unarmed placements: a refused digest's first issue and a disposed digest's explicit reissue. Continuation completion alone releases no unscanned output; under abandonment clearing the gate resumes nothing of the abandoned setup. twr-ggw.23 supplies the disposed-digest cross-check and refusal outcomes [ARC-43, SEC-5, CNF-95].

- [ ] The harness-output exemption applies only to ARC-43's unarmed-reference barrier. It never exempts a command from STA-20's unresolved-command hold or STA-24's destructive stop [ARC-43, STA-20, STA-24].

title: Enrol the operator's relay key with the publisher's first-stage relay
description:
## What to build
The harness shows the derived relay public key and pass index for out-of-band handoff, and the publisher records the pass by hand with its destinations and expiry; nothing secret crosses and nothing is pasted into the app. paid-tcp-relay's test set, run against that relay, passes its handshake, destination and private-address cases, and the harness's relay client from twr-ggw.3, under the derived relay key twr-ggw.11 wires in, connects through it to a destination the publisher recorded for the test.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The harness shows the relay public key and pass index, and no secret is shown or pasted [STG-18, CHN-15].
- [ ] Record the relay implementation repository, exact implementation commit and build inputs, deployed artifact digest, and that implementation's passing executable conformance record at the paid-tcp-relay revision selected by tau-web CHN-15, using the selected **/v2/** profile. Use merged paid-tcp-relay revision `49309df54dea3841f3cb1a37527f8d4ec9b5f1ab`, selected by tau-web `03fce703202cdf667a19c47a7131f5ed45afa63f` CHN-15. Map the record to every applicable stage-1 obligation of tau-web CNF-81/CNF-87: paid-tcp-relay CNF-3, CNF-4, CNF-5, CNF-10, CNF-12, CNF-13, CNF-14, CNF-9's hand-retirement/destination-removal cases, and CNF-21 where publisher discovery is offered. Include the publisher hosting profile's applicable no-log, TLS and independent-egress evidence (R CNF-16/CNF-19 and T CNF-113), with no additional retained-state allowance, relay-side environment exclusions, the precisely declared private DNS TCP/53 exception and observation scope explicit. Each guarded property needs a control showing its check fails when broken. This is the implementation's suite/evidence, not an executable test set supplied by the specification or its wire/discovery fixture files. For CNF-4, observe outbound initiation at the relay during refused AUTH, with a positive control that detects a deliberately early attempt even if the destination accepts nothing; separately observe no application bytes reaching the destination before OK. List deployment-dependent self-address inventory, effective egress, admitted TLS/capture/collection path and retained-store inspections as separate assertions with their own evidence/status. Source/static checks and isolated tests alone never establish them.
- [ ] Separately run and record the client-observable integration matrix against the **live relay public base** and controlled, recorded destinations, using /v2/ and the relay's configured timing limits: challenge/AUTH/OK ordering and admission refusals, recorded-only reachability, arbitrary-port access and pacing, and required /v2/ frame/termination behavior observable by the selected client API. “Supported” behavior does not narrow the selected protocol. Include controlled receiver observations for no byte before OK where the setup permits; attribute every assertion to its actual observation point, with observation controls. Client refusals/timeouts do not prove no outbound attempt before AUTH, application private-address refusal, absence of retained logs or independent egress enforcement. No live-service loopback/private listeners, fixture pause controls or internal event logs are assumed. Adapt reusable client cases explicitly; do not relabel the ce2097c/844e834 v1 fixture matrix as a live /v2/ record.

Both records identify the same implementation/artifact under test. The live record cites a deployment record binding its public base to the running artifact digest and effective configuration; equality of source commits alone is insufficient. Reference existing correctly bound relay/consumer records where appropriate. Include CNF-87's separate CHN-19/SEC-8 publisher discovery and recovery evidence, not just a successful TCP connection or fetched list. Keep OPR-4/CNF-81's self-host-migration demonstrations deferred until that capability is enabled; this does not defer the applicable CNF-21 publisher-discovery move/alias duties. Purchase, signed destination recording and signed revocation remain outside stage 1; the existing signed-revocation gate before paid/public access remains intact.

For every required assertion, record either passing evidence at its required observation point or an explicit pending status and named admission blocker. An unavailable live repetition does not invalidate a property already adequately demonstrated by correctly bound evidence at its required observation point; it also cannot replace genuinely live/deployment-required evidence. Criterion 2, CNF-81/CNF-87 and publisher-hosting admission cannot be reported passed while any required deployment or live assertion remains pending. Keep local results recordable without claiming admission. The relay evidence introduction in tau-web 07-conformance.md says "Changes to the effective artifact/configuration, network path/policy, capture/collection components, address inventory, TLS or relevant retained state invalidate affected evidence and require re-demonstration."
- [ ] The harness connects through the relay to the recorded test destination under the derived relay key [CNF-87, CHN-16].

title: Exporting and importing the recovery sheet
description:
## What to build
A passphrase-wrapped payload v3 carries allocations with tombstones, host-key pins with their routes, the exposure ledger, machine states with installation status and applications, placements, and the inference account credential, and the export screen states what the sheet can do in the wrong hands. Import runs CNF-84's refusal matrix before binding, and round trips show the exporter never writes a sheet its own import refuses. A maintained cloud machine's setup does not complete until the sheet is saved.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The sheet carries STA-16's contents and no value, digest, scan key or byte length; applications use the explicit empty list and the no-model marker [STA-16, CNF-84].
- [ ] The export screen says that the sheet, with its passphrase, can spend the remaining inference balance [CNF-19, STA-16].
- [ ] A maintained cloud machine's setup does not complete without a saved sheet [CNF-19, STA-15].
- [ ] The exposure ledger is exported [CNF-10 (export)].
- [ ] Import refuses, before binding: a mismatched seed, duplicate mappings, invalid counters, a live machine with a missing, duplicate or malformed machine state, malformed placement associations, malformed application or provider data, two applications with one name on one machine, and payload versions 1 and 2 [CNF-84 (refusals), STA-22b].
- [ ] Machines with and without applications, including one without a model of its own, round-trip through export and import [CNF-84 (round trip)].
- [ ] An imported local-store backup's machines show unchecked, their findings unknown, and refuse a placement until a re-check [CNF-84, STA-22b].
- [ ] Every imported seed, from a current or stale sheet or an imported local-store backup, restores only listed identities and refuses every new allocation in every family, regardless of ceremony record; a bare seed with neither is refused before binding, explaining that it restores nothing and offering the sheet or a fresh start [STA-22b, CNF-84].
- [ ] A CHN-R7 pin round-trips with its `lnvps_retrieve` route and retrieval disclosure, and with its machine's installation groups: incomplete and refused observations, an initial empty group opened by a job read or attest, empty reinstall boundaries, and each source's active or retired pins [CNF-84, CNF-109].
- [ ] The import path journals the restriction: after a worker restart and replay, allocation is refused in every family, under a test that restarts the worker [STA-22b] (from twr-ggw.59).
- [ ] An import killed at each storage operation reopens refused or incomplete, never as a store that allocates, and never falls through to a freshly generated seed (`Store::finish_creation`) [STA-22b] (from twr-ggw.59).
- [ ] Replay refuses a restore record anywhere the import path does not put it [STA-22b] (from twr-ggw.59).

- [ ] Round-trip the required seed_backup member: none, or one seed_id-bound full_reentry/skipped completion. Refuse missing, malformed, duplicate records/object members, unknown completion and mismatched seed id before binding. Restore journals the record or explicit absence, imported seeds owe no ceremony, and Replace clears it. The sheet remains payload v3; round-trip version-2 declarations and retain installation ordinals through Replace [STA-16, STA-23, STA-17, CNF-84; docs/design/credential-format-v1.md].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.72 — requirements at spec 8869ade
- twr-ggw.6 — Allocation: an index is journaled before use and never reused
- twr-ggw.11 — Binding: a session holds only its bound machine's key
- twr-ggw.15 — The delivery declaration is proposed, approved and journaled before anything is installed
- twr-ggw.17 — Procured inference: recorded calls under a capped session inference key
- twr-ggw.23 — place_secret places an application secret, scanned in the placing session

## Spec
STA-15, STA-16, STA-22a, STA-22b, ADR-0040, CNF-10, CNF-19, CNF-84, CNF-109, CHN-R7, STA-17, STA-23

title: Restore: reconnect on old host-key pins, unknown since export, re-arm before output
description:
## What to build
A seed plus sheet re-derives the same keys and reconnects each restored machine on its old host-key pin with no first contact, presented as non-revoking. Restored state is labelled "unknown since export" and restated at later irreversible acts until reapproved, applications are labelled "as of export", and machines show as unchecked, with placement refused before a re-check. Each recorded placement is re-armed from a machine report or the local paste fallback before output is released.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Restored machines reconnect on their old host-key pins with no new first contact, and the flow says it does not revoke [CNF-84 (reconnect), STA-17].
- [ ] A restored CHN-R7 pin reconnects only after the vendor's current published set reads complete and equal to it; with an empty or different set, or the status read failing, no contact is made, no pin is retired and no new first contact opens, and the machine is unresolved until the operator chooses a reinstall or abandonment [CNF-84, CNF-109].
- [ ] Restored placement state, declaration, class, access model and weaker modes are labelled "unknown since export" and restated at later irreversible acts, a place_secret card among them, until reapproved [CNF-84 (labels), STA-16].
- [ ] Applications are labelled "as of export", and a restored provider is listed beside its application only where a restored placement names that application [CNF-84, STA-16, TRU-E12].
- [ ] Each machine shows unchecked, its findings unknown, and refuses placement before a re-check [CNF-84, CNF-99, ARC-17].
- [ ] Every placement the sheet records on the bound set is re-armed by a machine report or the local paste fallback before output collection or model commands; a machine-derived reference is labelled "re-armed from the machine's report", never "protected" [CNF-95 (c), ARC-43].
- [ ] The post-export question has nothing preselected, "Not sure" yields unknown coverage, and the trust display keeps the sheet's placement entries [CNF-95, CNF-42 (Restore)].

- [ ] Restore uses twr-ggw.25's immediate local paste fallback and one-act post-reinstall re-read, with twr-ggw.23's disposed-digest cross-check and unarmed outcomes; neither local re-arm route reapproves restored state or lifts STA-20's unresolved-command hold or STA-24's destructive stop [ARC-43, SEC-5, CNF-95, STA-20, STA-24].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.25 — Re-arm in a later session, and the local paste fallback
- twr-ggw.27 — Exporting and importing the recovery sheet

## Spec
STA-16, STA-17, ARC-17, ARC-43, TRU-E12, CNF-42, CNF-84, CNF-95, CNF-109, SEC-5, STA-20, STA-24

title: Replace: rekey every machine under a new seed, and retire the relay pass by hand
description:
## What to build
A model-free flow states up front that both seeds and the old allocation metadata are needed, then for each machine re-enters with the old key and host-key pin, installs the new key, confirms a connection under it, and only then removes the old one. The new relay key is handed over out of band, and the old pass is not shown as retired until the publisher's confirmation is recorded; machine migration and pass retirement are interrupted separately, and neither partial result is reported complete. Replace names what it cannot fix and ends with the new seed's sheet; the live confirmation runs in twr-ggw.52.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The flow is model-free, and no session holds either key [CNF-20, STA-17, SEC-1].
- [ ] The old key is removed only after a connection authenticated by the new one, and a failed confirmation leaves it in place [CNF-20].
- [ ] An interrupted migration is never reported complete [CNF-20, CNF-84 (partial Replace)].
- [ ] The old pass is not shown retired before the publisher's confirmation is recorded, and an interrupted retirement is reported incomplete, separately from machine migration [CNF-20 (relay half), STA-17].
- [ ] The screen names application-secret rotation at its service, the unrevocable inference account credential, and possible thief persistence with a destroy-or-rebuild offer, and never describes re-arming as a remedy [CNF-20].
- [ ] Replace ends with the new seed's sheet, which a later import accepts and the old sheet no longer matches; machines show as having no current sheet until it is saved [CNF-20, STA-17].
- [ ] Generating Replace's fresh seed is never gated; all its machine-migration and new-pass allocations wait for that seed's durable ceremony record, after which allocation starts at zero [STA-22b, STA-23, CNF-72, CNF-84].
- [ ] Replace passes a freshly generated seed to the core, and a test shows that a Replace to a seed used before cannot reissue an identity; nothing relies on the core's guard as a freshness check [STA-17, STA-22b] (from twr-ggw.59).

- [ ] Carry the installation ordinal while moving the machine component to its new index. Refuse migration of an install unfinished in rescue through confirmation of the installed-system reset, including after pins are recorded; name it as not migrated, explain why and keep Replace incomplete. The dedicated relabel job and its dedicated evidence belong to twr-i6k.9; LNVPS writes no label [STA-17, STG-20, ARC-7, SEC-1, CNF-86].

- [ ] Under each of destructive reinstall and abandonment, refuse Replace's key install and old-key removal before dispatch, whoever starts it and whatever call was disposed. Status queries admitted by STA-24, pinned SSH attempts and record collection remain permitted and end no restriction; a harness-composed box-plane read is a command [STA-24, CNF-110, ADR-0050].

- [ ] Exercise CNF-40's held-harness-job case for Replace's key install and old-key removal: STA-20's unresolved-command hold records no intent and queues no job; the visible flow composes a first issue afresh after release, once under one intent. Stopping its wait leaves nothing armed through replay; only an operator act resumes that stopped flow [STA-20, CNF-40].

- [ ] A machine under STA-20's unresolved-command hold or a standing destructive reinstall or abandonment disposition is shown as not yet migrated, with its reason and its old key kept, while Replace migrates the others. After admission returns, migration starts with the key install as a first issue in the prescribed order; Replace remains incomplete while any machine is outstanding [STA-17, STA-20, STA-24, CNF-20].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.58 — prerequisite behaviour used by these criteria
- twr-ggw.72 — requirements at spec 8869ade
- twr-ggw.27 — Exporting and importing the recovery sheet

## Spec
STA-17, SEC-1, ADR-0040, CNF-20, CNF-84, ARC-7, CNF-72, CNF-86, STA-22b, STA-23, STG-20, ADR-0050, CNF-110, CNF-40, STA-20, STA-24

title: The paid-tcp-relay handshake matrix on the relay fixture
description:
## What to build
The relay fixture grows paid-tcp-relay's full handshake, and the harness's relay client passes CNF-87's handshake items against it. These are the fixture half of CNF-87; the same test set runs against the publisher's relay in twr-ggw.26.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A stale challenge, an unknown key and a replayed signature are each refused [CNF-87, WIR-4–WIR-10].
- [ ] Only the recorded destination set is reachable, and the relay's timing limits from the bundle are applied [CNF-87].
- [ ] The order challenge, AUTH, OK holds; a binary frame before OK, or a text frame after it, closes the socket [CNF-87].
- [ ] The fixture records no dial before the AUTH is accepted and no byte before OK [CNF-87].
- [ ] The client signs with a relay key the test supplies; twr-ggw.11 replaces it with the derived relay key.

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.2 — Tracer bullet: one recorded command over a pinned SSH connection through a relay fixture

## Spec
CHN-15, CHN-16, WIR-4–WIR-10, CNF-87

title: An unfinished setup owns the first screen; abandonment where the vendor offers no destroy route
description:
## What to build
Resume-or-abandon is the opening screen, with what has been billed and what bills monthly. Abandonment is the deterministic operator flow, outside any session: it destroys through typed operations where the vendor offers the operator a destroy route, and on a fixture adapter with stop, renewal control and reinstall but no destroy it applies ARC-22's treatment. A Restore that finds a cloud machine with no sheet offers that treatment, never an unpinned login.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The opening screen is resume-or-abandon, with billed-so-far and the monthly cost [ARC-22].
- [ ] Abandonment runs as the deterministic operator flow, never through a session, and against a machine with an unresolved call it is a disposition [ARC-21, STA-24].
- [ ] On the no-destroy fixture adapter it stops the machine, turns renewal off and shows it as "still existing and billed until the vendor's stated deletion date" [ARC-22].
- [ ] It names an unresolved create that no listing matches as possibly still existing and billing, and the listing runs as a read [ARC-22, STA-24].
- [ ] Where the harness would recreate a machine, it offers a reinstall as a new first contact that the old host-key pin does not admit [ARC-22].
- [ ] A cloud machine found with no sheet is offered this treatment, never an unpinned keyed-rescue login [CNF-84 (no-sheet clause), STA-15].
- [ ] Abandonment dispatches as the deterministic operator flow outside any session, at "the destroy, or the stop that stands in for it" naming the machine: the disposition's restriction ends at that operation's durably appended intent and not before; from that intent its own barrier refuses and nothing is refused under the disposition [CNF-110, STA-24, ARC-21, ARC-22].

title: Service lifecycle findings
description:
## What to build
Unit-state and enablement reads validate ARC-43's service grammar and the declaration's scope, and use ARC-43's operator-chosen reboot evidence. A declared service outside its declared lifecycle is a lifecycle finding, which never refuses placement on its own. CNF-53's cases (a) to (d) pass. Case (e), at re-entry, is twr-ggw.50's; twr-ggw.73 adds the decided running-at-delivery boot-anchor cases.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] For stage-1 systemd reads, require a bare name matching ^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9:_.-]*$ of at most 247 bytes; append .service, pass -- and preserve wrapper quoting. Refuse @ instances and unsupported suffixes. Validate declaration v2 scope and user-account grammar; use the named user's manager and require Linger=yes, never substitute a system-manager read. Refuse invalid inputs before composing a read [ARC-43, CNF-107; docs/design/delivery-declaration-v1.md].
- [ ] After the last placement, offer a reboot only with an enabled-survives-reboot service and no co-declared running-at-delivery service. Require the operator's explicit yes then, record old boot identity, reboot, reconnect on the pin, confirm a new boot identity and active unit, then check delivery before any model command. At LNVPS use typed restart and its vendor barrier; until T50 defines confirmation, exercise after its continuing disposition, never use the boot read to clear the cloud barrier. The harness-only delivery_reboot job and its dedicated-row settlement and pending-delivery-check cases belong to twr-i6k.11 [ARC-43, STA-24, CNF-53, T50].
- [ ] CNF-53 (a) to (d) pass [CNF-53].
- [ ] A lifecycle finding beside any other finding still refuses placement, and a finding's class comes from the declaration field that produced it [CNF-94, ARC-17].

- [ ] If no reboot is demonstrated, including decline or co-declared running-at-delivery, keep an otherwise Delivered machine with enabled, restart not demonstrated beside every Delivered on card/trust display, no lifecycle finding. A changed boot identity plus re-check lifts it. A dropped boot restriction is a finding; a user unit without Linger=yes is still a lifecycle finding. Exercise every stage-1 CNF-53 case; twr-ggw.50 owns the later re-entry offer and twr-ggw.73 the boot-anchor cases [ARC-17, ARC-43, SEC-6, CNF-44, CNF-53].

- [ ] Under each of destructive reinstall and abandonment, refuse service-state, enablement and boot-identity delivery-check reads before dispatch, whoever starts it and whatever call was disposed. Status queries admitted by STA-24, pinned SSH attempts and record collection remain permitted and end no restriction; a harness-composed box-plane read is a command [STA-24, CNF-110, ADR-0050].

- [ ] Exercise CNF-40's held-harness-job case for service-state, enablement and boot-identity delivery-check reads: STA-20's unresolved-command hold records no intent and queues no job; the visible flow composes a first issue afresh after release, once under one intent. Stopping its wait leaves nothing armed through replay; only an operator act resumes that stopped flow [STA-20, CNF-40].

- [ ] At LNVPS refuse delivery_reboot's own-record settlement for typed restart; a boot read never confirms a vendor operation. After the yes journaled with the typed restart intent, ARC-43's pending-delivery-check hold bars commands through the delivery verdict, including after restart settlement. A stopped pending check journals its stop and shows stopped, never pass; disposing a delivery-read command to continue releases only STA-20's unresolved-command hold. An exec of the same reboot bytes remains an ordinary command, settling by exit and unresolved after Ended or incomplete evidence [ARC-43, STA-20, STA-24, CNF-53, CNF-55].

- [ ] The applicability row fixes this split, including ARC-43's pending-delivery-check hold: “LNVPS's typed-restart survival evidence, its typed-restart settlement refusal, its typed-restart hold after the journaled yes including after the reboot settled, its typed-restart stopped pending-check case, the `exec` of the same reboot bytes and every other item-53 case stay here.” Item 55's delivery_reboot settlement belongs to twr-i6k.11; ordinary record persistence remains stage 1 [CNF-53, CNF-55].
