## Prerequisite uptake at 66762f1

Reuse this ticket for the specification-pin prerequisite of twr-ggw.23. Land the prerequisite separately from main before rebuilding the placement branch. Target specification commit: 66762f1a63f43977f4ef407c194a73e1ae71458a, descending from the current d029ebd pin and carrying the adapter-predicate amendment 4be3cda.

The witness change is behavioral: schema 7 adds receipt bindings to approvals and calls, received-result events, retained receipts, and the orderAssociation guard. The current comparison names the removed v6 file, accepts only schema 6 and has no receipt vocabulary; the current dispatch and journal have no corresponding receipt settlement. Changing only the filename or accepting and discarding new members is insufficient.

STA-24 at 4be3cda says:

> Confirmation evidence MUST identify the expected account, machine and operation and be durably
> appended before taking effect. Failed append, timeout and operator disposition establish no success.
> Receipt evidence binds the successful response to the exact dispatched call, signed request,
> account and target, received over browser-terminated vendor TLS, with its operation-specific
> interpretation. A generic 2xx, an unrelated response or an unvalidated/malformed body is
> insufficient. Receipt authority is limited to order, stop and restart;
> no other mutation response becomes confirmation.

STG-21a at 4be3cda says:

> A validated recorded response correlated to the order confirms its returned VM id, durably associated with the approved entry. Order confirmation establishes the vendor order's returned or reconciled VM id and its association with the approved entry. It does not establish host creation, IP allocation, invoice production, payment, boot or contact readiness. Zero inventory matches leaves unresolved, never proves non-execution and never authorises another order; unpaid purge is one reason. Conflicting/multiple candidates require inspection and no automatic association. Exact account, client SSH key, image and full template/custom resources must be checked against the original recorded intent, and the selected id must not already belong to another entry. No automatic start route or history-based confirmation is added.

## Additional acceptance for schema 7

- Advance the gitlink on this ticket's branch and commit the new pin before gates that resolve it from HEAD. Preserve the saved placement branch and its pin-only commit.
- Add the shared dispatch and durable-journal behavior for operation-limited receipt confirmation. Correlate approved binding, call, target, resource, account, signed request and operation; retain provenance and validation. Robot and unbound approvals, reinstall receipts and non-vendor sources cannot gain receipt authority.
- An order requires its returned id and matching durable approved-entry association as well as its durable receipt. Test both record arrival orders, missing id, missing/wrong association, failed receipt/association append and replay; neither half alone settles it. Stop confirmation establishes stopped state only, without destruction or billing cessation.
- Consume all new v7 receipt witnesses through the real dispatch/store path. Compare each applicable start, outcome and projection, including retained receipts and settled calls. Preserve closed vocabulary checks, every existing partition and all 470 enumerated traces. Schema 7 carries 110 named traces, including 13 new receipt traces; none may be silently skipped or renamed a read.
- Demonstrate meaningful negative controls for correlation and the order-association guard, and verify old records retain their prior meaning through replay. Required offline host/web gates and the complete fixture tracer pass unpiped. A browser startup failure gives no browser-case credit.
- Record the whole pin delta and affected open-ticket citations. Keep the complete LNVPS adapter predicates with their existing consumers (.32/.40/.41/.43/.45/.48); shared receipt adoption establishes no live adapter completion. Package-policy follow-through stays with .79/.80 and its disclosure/admission/native-evidence consumers. Hidden-session/Lock follow-through stays with the already assigned .89. Protected-evidence and placement implementation stays with .23. Do not close these owners or claim their conformance merely because this pin lands.

## Verification boundary

Use fixture-only evidence. No live vendor operation, CORS-probe execution, spending, cluster access or deployment is authorized by this prerequisite. The existing CI gate definitions remain required for later publication; offline local evidence does not establish live reachability. Do not alter placement implementation or replay its saved draft.

title: The seed derives roles 0–4 and matches every v1 vector
description:
## What to build

Derivation matches the v1 credential vectors, the upstream BIP-32 and RFC 8032 vectors, and a second implementation, and an invalid child, an unknown version or an out-of-range index is refused, never aliased. Every credential type in the code names its SEC-5 row.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Different roles and indices yield distinct keys; an out-of-range index, an unknown version and an invalid child each fail rather than alias a valid allocation [CNF-83].
- [ ] The mnemonic passphrase is empty whatever the local unlock passphrase is [CNF-83].
- [ ] Each credential type in the code maps to a SEC-5 row, and a type with no row fails a test [CNF-13].

comments.text:
Done on a28130c, accepted by the Run's Panel and Manager after two Rounds.

- src/seed.rs: BIP-39 generate (16 bytes from getrandom) and import (12 English words exactly, ASCII whitespace tolerated, valid checksum); the seed by PBKDF2 with salt "mnemonic" through a function that takes no passphrase; the seed identifier; hardened BIP-32 derivation of roles 0-4 at m/707285'/1'/role'/index'. An unknown version, a role outside 0-4, an index above 2^31-1 and an invalid first step or child are each refused, never aliased or skipped (STA-22, STA-22a).
- src/credential.rs: a sealed Credential trait giving each type its SEC-5 row: Seed 15, SshClientKey 3, AttestSenderKey 7, AttestRecipientKey 16, RelayKey 4, PostHarnessCredential 17, HostKeyPin 5. Credentials, PinSource and testonly's test keys now hand out these types.
- CNF-83 evidence (cargo test): the v1 known answers read from spec/ at the pin (seed, seed_id, all 10 vectors); BIP-32 vectors 1, 3, 4 and 5 (key-range entries refused, 14 serialization entries listed as not applicable); RFC 8032 section 7.1; BIP-340 public keys; the BIP-39 reference vectors; the bip39 and bip32 crates as a host-only second implementation on 18 entropies, every role, indices up to 2^31-1; distinct keys; refusals; the empty passphrase; generate round trip.
- CNF-13 evidence: every registered type checked against SEC-5 parsed from the pinned tree; a syn scan of src/ fails on an unregistered type holding key material, including a const-length u8 array, and refuses a name defined twice.
- Gates on the final tree (Manager, Rust 1.97.1): fmt 0, clippy -D warnings 0, cargo test 0 (51 tests), cors-probe 0, check-install-disks 0, --baseline 1, wasm32 clippy served 0 and tracer 0, check-adr-0024 0. Reviewers also ran the served build's check-absence and check-csp, and tracer.sh: all 0.
- Mutation proofs: each turned a named test red and was restored. title: LNVPS stop and renewal-off, and the adapter's origin
description:
## What to build
Stop and automatic-renewal-off are journaled before send and confirmed only by predicates supplied by the still-open T50 contract; a lost response stays unresolved and a second request is refused. At a fixture LNVPS they drive twr-ggw.31's treatment, including deletion confirmed as the spec defines it. The LNVPS origin's route is chosen by a no-side-effect probe before any side-effecting call.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Killing the worker between record and send leaves the stop's and the renewal-off's records [CNF-28].
- [ ] Each is confirmed only by its predicate; with its response lost it stays unresolved, and a second request under a new call id is refused [CNF-29, STA-24, STA-5].
- [ ] Abandonment at the fixture LNVPS stops the machine, turns renewal off, and shows it as existing and billed until deletion is confirmed by the spec's predicate [ARC-22].
- [ ] Rules that end at a destroy keep running after a stop, since ARC-22 says "A stop is neither confirmed destruction nor confirmed billing cessation" [ARC-22, SEC-1, SEC-5].
- [ ] A recreate or a Replace rebuild's old machine at the fixture LNVPS takes this treatment [CNF-84 (cloud recreate at LNVPS)].
- [ ] The LNVPS origin's route is chosen by a no-side-effect probe before any side-effecting call, and the CORS probe covering that origin fails the build when it fails [CNF-32 (LNVPS), CNF-4, ARC-34].
- [ ] At LNVPS, the abandonment continuation is dispatched at the stop that stands in for a destroy: the restriction ends at its durably appended intent and not before, "from then on that call's own barrier governs", and nothing is refused under the disposition; renewal-off and a status read do not end the standing restriction [CNF-110, STA-24, ARC-22].
- [ ] With an unresolved LNVPS stop disposed toward abandonment, the model's box-plane command to that machine and every cloud-plane operation within the disposed calls' reach outside the abandonment flow are refused: "abandonment only the abandonment flow" [CNF-110, STA-24, ARC-22].

- [ ] At dispatch the abandonment flow authorizes only machines whose vendor id reached this unfinished setup's approved entry through its own create response or admissible evidence tied to the seed-derived key. An imported sheet mapping alone is refused; exercise refusal and admission with identical ids but different evidence [SEC-4, CNF-26, ARC-21].

- [ ] The flow's destroy/stop waits for a disposition naming every unresolved call; an omitted unresolved call keeps barring it. With no unresolved call no disposition is needed. A session destroy/stop under standing abandonment is refused even when its binding is valid [STA-24, CNF-110].

- [ ] Renewal-off waits for the stop's own confirmation, never a job-record or boot-identity substitute. Until T50 defines the observation, leave the stop unresolved until evidence or disposition; test that unresolved stop refuses renewal-off [STA-24, CNF-110, T50].

- [ ] At LNVPS, the stop that stands in for a destroy, its later renewal-off, a reinstall and absence of a file end no placed-secret listing or scan-reference duty. Keep P1/P2 listed and counted until rotation or the vendor's confirmed deletion, not the stop. Confirmation uses the vendor's deletion contract, still owed by T50, never a job or boot report; supply this result to twr-ggw.23's placement ledger and twr-ggw.25's fallback card [SEC-5, SEC-6, ARC-43, CNF-42, CNF-95, T50].

title: Ordering an LNVPS machine over HTTP after the operator's verification, and its invoice
description:
## What to build
Before the first order under a machine's identity, the LNVPS adapter submits the operator's own email address to that account at the vendor, tells the operator that LNVPS mails a single-use link valid for about a day, and waits until the account reads as verified; only then does it submit the machine's HTTP order (STG-21). The order is journaled before it is sent; a lost response leaves it unresolved and a second order is refused. The wallet's invoice comes over TLS from the vendor's recorded order or renew response (ARC-30), shown on CNF-104's distinct fixture invoices.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The operator's address is submitted to the vendor and nowhere else, the same address serves every machine's account, and the harness creates no mailbox and reads no mail [STG-21].
- [ ] No order is submitted until the account reads as verified [STG-21].
- [ ] The order is journaled before it is sent, and killing the worker between record and send leaves the record [CNF-28, SEC-12].
- [ ] With the response lost the order stays unresolved, and a second order for the entry under a new call id or a second index is refused [CNF-29 (LNVPS create), STA-24].
- [ ] Successful vendor-TLS reads from an order response and from a renew response each hand that response's invoice to the wallet, tied to the approved entry, its amount beside the approved cost [CNF-104, ARC-30].
- [ ] When neither response supplies an invoice, none reaches the wallet [CNF-104, ARC-30].
- [ ] After each order the machine's automatic renewal is turned off and read back off before the machine is offered for delivery; a fixture vendor reporting it on is set off [STG-21, CNF-104].
- [ ] A different invoice presented in model text never reaches the wallet [CNF-104].
- [ ] Every standing mode is restated at the paid invoice [CNF-93 (paid invoice)].
- [ ] With an unresolved LNVPS order (create) disposed under either continuation that continues, a box-plane command is dispatched; with that call disposed toward a destructive reinstall or abandonment, the model's command is refused, "whatever the disposed call was" [CNF-110, STA-24].

title: Pinning an LNVPS machine from its published host keys
description:
## What to build
The published host keys are read over TLS and journaled with their route, under the route T39 admits, and the first contact must present a published key or halt. The host-key pin's route is written to the sheet and restored by import. The host-pin core runs the companion comparison against the re-emitted pins witness file.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The host keys are read over TLS from the fixture vendor and journaled with their route before any connection [SEC-5 row 5, ARC-43].
- [ ] No connection is made until the admitted route's condition at the spec pin holds, and the wait uses the bundle's named timing [T39, OPN-24].
- [ ] A first contact presenting a key other than the journaled one halts [CNF-21, SEC-11].
- [ ] A machine whose published key set never fills is handled as CNF-23's no-keys case states at the spec pin [CNF-23].
- [ ] The host-key pin's route is exported in the sheet and restored by import [CNF-84 (pin routes), STA-16].
- [ ] CNF-109's published-route cases pass: only the recorded machine status response, fetched directly over browser-terminated TLS, is read, and only its published host-key field becomes an installed-system pin; a set is admitted only when complete; a presented key outside the pin halts on first and on later contact; a partial reading completed in the same installation, a contradictory complete candidate, and overlap with an earlier installation's incomplete, refused or older observation; refused observations stay in the comparison history; repeated empty, exact, reordered and subset readings do not grow it; another machine's history neither blocks nor admits this one [CNF-109, SEC-11].
- [ ] CNF-109's cross-source history cases pass with the earlier pin seeded by importing a fixture sheet (twr-ggw.27), since stage 1 produces neither source: overlap with an earlier job-read or attest pin, an exact old job-pin repeat, a disjoint publication after a job pin; and without a reinstall no source replaces an active installed pin [CNF-109, CNF-84].
- [ ] The trust display labels the pin "retrieved from the vendor's hypervisor scan", never attested, and states its residual as "the vendor, and anyone able to answer on the machine's address inside the vendor's network at scan time"; the disclosure and every refusal block this route [CNF-109, CHN-R7, TRU-E1, TRU-E13].
- [ ] The host-pin core passes the companion comparison over the twr-ggw.43 bucket of pins-witnesses-v5.json, schema 5: 39 witnesses and 2185 enumerated traces at `8869ade`. Implementation reading: a leading pinned attest or ready_to_reset step admitted by step 2 stands for a pin a Restore brought in. Load the knowledge after the last leading step as imported fixture state, retaining pin provenance, installation groups and introduction consumption, and compare from the next step. This tests no fresh job-read or attest admission. This seeds 1 witness and 100 enumerated traces with leading attest, and 5 witnesses and 200 enumerated traces with leading ready_to_reset. Credential-format-v1.md allows historical attest pins to reconstruct consumed introductions even when retired. The integrated cross-source cases use fixture-sheet Restore. Seeded knowledge that Restore cannot carry is a BLOCK naming the trace. Use this single decision list, written so it can be pasted into the test, first match wins. Step 1: a trace holding reset or rescue_last goes to the attest row if it also holds attest, otherwise to twr-i6k.3. Step 2: otherwise send it to twr-ggw.43 if it holds neither attest nor ready_to_reset, or if all attest/ready_to_reset steps are a pinned leading prefix followed by a published step. Step 3: otherwise send a trace holding attest to the attest row. Step 4: otherwise send it to twr-i6k.3. Read start records before the first step. Unknown schema, event kind, outcome or projection member fails naming the trace. Compare every owned outcome and knowledge projection at every step; each refused/admitted pair stays whole. At 8869ade the buckets sum to 75 witnesses and 8421 enumerated traces, bound 3 over 20: twr-ggw.43 has 39 / 2185, twr-i6k.3 has 21 / 4090, and the outstanding attest row has 15 / 2146. The file's bound is covered only by twr-ggw.43's and twr-i6k.3's runs together with the attest row's run, which is outstanding; deferral enables nothing. All 832 enumerated rescue-plus-attest traces (no named witnesses hold both) go to attest, with every step left to that run. The record names the rule, file, bound, spec and implementation revisions. CNF-3's three breaks each turn this comparison red, naming the trace, made once by hand and recorded here: flip an expected outcome in a scratch file; remove or empty the file; supply an unrecognised event kind or outcome [CNF-3, CNF-84, CNF-109, ADR-0032].

```python
def pins(trace):
    steps=trace['steps']; kinds={s['event']['kind'] for s in steps}
    if kinds & {'reset','rescue_last'}:
        return 'attest' if 'attest' in kinds else 'dedicated'
    sources=[n for n,s in enumerate(steps) if s['event']['kind'] in ('attest','ready_to_reset')]
    if not sources: return 'stage1'
    if sources==list(range(len(sources))) and all(steps[n]['pinned'] for n in sources) and any(
        s['event']['kind']=='published' for s in steps[len(sources):]):
        return 'stage1'
    if 'attest' in kinds: return 'attest'
    return 'dedicated'
```

title: LNVPS reinstall: a new first contact
description:
## What to build
A reinstall is journaled before send, stops box-plane dispatch to the machine until its confirmation or a disposition, and is confirmed only by the predicate the spec pin carries. It is restated with the standing modes, and it retires the old host-key pin, so the reinstalled system is reached only through a new first contact on twr-ggw.43's route. The recovery ladder's third rung at LNVPS takes the form the spec pin decides.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Killing the worker between record and send leaves the reinstall's record [CNF-28].
- [ ] With its response lost it stays unresolved, and a second request under a new call id is refused [CNF-29, STA-24].
- [ ] From its intent until confirmation or a disposition, no box-plane command is dispatched to the machine [STA-24].
- [ ] Every standing mode is restated at the reinstall [CNF-93 (reinstall), SEC-14].
- [ ] The old host-key pin does not admit the reinstalled system; the first contact waits for the route's new capture and halts on a mismatch [ARC-22, CNF-84 (reinstall), SEC-11].
- [ ] The reinstall retires every source's installed pin, imported job-read and attest pins included, and opens a distinct installation group even when its first reading is empty; the groups survive a restart, and a new complete publication can then pin under CHN-R7 [CNF-109].
- [ ] The ladder's third rung at LNVPS takes the form the spec pin states [ARC-16, STG-17].
- [ ] Under a standing destructive-reinstall disposition at LNVPS, "the vendor's reinstall call" is the dispatch of the continuation: the restriction ends at its durably appended intent and not before; from that intent its own barrier refuses and nothing is refused under the disposition [CNF-110, STA-24, ARC-22].
- [ ] Under a standing abandonment disposition whose disposed calls barred the reinstall, the LNVPS reinstall is refused: "A destructive reinstall permits only the reinstall, abandonment only the abandonment flow" [CNF-110, STA-24, ARC-22].

- [ ] Retire the old pin and advance the installation only at vendor reinstall dispatch, never at choosing or recording a disposition. Restart and Restore open no installation [CHN-R7, STG-20, CNF-109].

title: The local store: unlock, append before apply, lock
description:
## What to build
The local passphrase unwraps a v1 envelope holding the seed inside the harness worker alone, and the tracer's in-memory journal gives way to the encrypted append-only journal, appended before apply. Reload, page hide, explicit lock and a killed worker each require a new unlock, after which replay runs. The persistent-storage request is made and its refusal shown.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A wrong passphrase, a modified envelope or record, a cross-store substitution and an unknown format each fail closed, and no new empty store replaces a failed decryption [CNF-82, STA-23].
- [ ] An event whose append fails is not applied [STA-3].
- [ ] Reload, page hide, explicit lock and a killed worker each require unlock again; session workers lose access, and replay keeps unresolved actions [CNF-82, STA-23].
- [ ] Persisted bytes and worker inputs hold no forbidden plaintext key; the passphrase reaches only the worker's unlock input and is cleared after use [CNF-82, SEC-5 row 18].
- [ ] No credential appears in cleartext in origin-private storage, local storage or service-worker caches [CNF-15, STG-10].
- [ ] The persistent-storage request is made, a refusal is shown, and the interface promises no immunity from loss [CNF-82, STA-23].

- twr-ggw.4 — The seed derives roles 0–4 and matches every v1 vector

description:

description:
## What

title: ARC-33's policy and the harness worker: does it bind the worker's context, and how does a static host deliver it?
description:
## What to build
Deliver the policy through the static host and admit workers only after their first-running self-check. The page's meta policy and the tracer's header alone do not satisfy this duty. Ship the deployment configuration or documented host setup with a check that fails when the policy is absent.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The static HTTPS host sends ARC-33's policy as a Content-Security-Policy response header covering worker scripts; a site-wide header suffices [ARC-32, ARC-33, ADR-0046].
- [ ] The page, harness worker and every session worker run under that policy however started. The self-check is the first thing each worker runs, before dependencies load; load dependencies afterwards by dynamic import [ARC-33].
- [ ] In the worker's own context, establish refusal of data-module import(), cross-origin-module import(), eval and Function. Do not rely on eval alone or a patchable global. Preserve the directive list; do not introduce a blob-worker inheritance shim [ARC-33, ADR-0046, CNF-111].
- [ ] With no response header, the harness worker refuses unlock with a visible reason. A session worker outside the policy refuses credentials with a reason. Show negative controls for both; no key or dependency reaches the worker first [ARC-33, CNF-111].
- [ ] With the policy present, wasm loads and the store opens. Run both controls in the integrated harness and retain evidence, including the session worker before it is enabled [CNF-111].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.2 — worker, served build and tracer
- twr-ggw.72 — worker policy requirements at the pin

## Spec
ARC-32, ARC-33, CNF-111, ADR-0046, STA-1, STA-23

## As filed (gap and question)

Kept verbatim as filed, at spec `ee133d0`: its quotations are that pin's, and its checkboxes are not live. The criteria above, at `8869ade`, supersede everything in this section.

## The gap

`ARC-33` sets the Content-Security-Policy that is "the boundary for code the harness never
meant to run": strict `script-src`, `object-src` and `base-uri`, permissive `connect-src`. It
does not say whether that policy must also bind the harness worker's own context. Nor does it
say how a static host delivers the policy to the worker (`ARC-32`: "served from a single
origin, as a static HTTPS host").

The two cases behave differently:

- **Page.** The served build (twr-ggw.2, commit 55dedb4) carries the policy in the page's
  `<meta>` element. That needs no host configuration.
- **Worker.** A dedicated worker loaded from an `https:` URL takes its policy from its own
  response headers, not from the page. A static host that sends no `Content-Security-Policy`
  header therefore leaves the harness worker with no policy at all. The harness worker is the
  context that holds keys, pins and the journal (`STA-1`, `STA-23`). The tracer only shows the
  policy enforced in the worker because its test server sends the header on `worker.js`. The
  README states this limit.

## The question for the specification

Does `ARC-33`'s policy bind the harness worker's context?
- **If it does:** how is it delivered from a static host? For example, a host configuration
  the repository ships, or a requirement on the host to send the header.
- **If it does not:** the corpus should say so, and say why the page's policy is enough.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The specification answers the question above, at a pin this repository adopts.
- [ ] The served build, or its documented deployment, follows that answer, with a check that
  fails when it does not.

title: The harness's relay client passes a text frame received after OK to SSH as bytes: does paid-tcp-relay's WIR-8 bind the client?
description:
## The gap

After the relay's `{"ok": true}`, the harness's relay client (`src/harness/run.rs`, from
twr-ggw.2 and twr-ggw.3, commit a0855f7) hands the WebSocket to SSH with ws_stream_wasm's
`into_io()`. In ws_stream_wasm 0.7.5, `From<WsMessage> for Vec<u8>` turns `WsMessage::Text(s)`
into its bytes. So a **text** frame the relay sends after OK enters the SSH byte stream as if it
were TCP bytes. Nothing ends the attempt.

paid-tcp-relay's `WIR-8` at `844e834` (the wire `CHN-15` adopts) says: "After `OK`, every frame in
both directions MUST be a binary frame carrying raw TCP. A text frame after `OK`, or a binary
frame before it, MUST close the connection with code 1002."

The impact is bounded. The SSH session is pinned end to end, so injected bytes can break the
session but cannot be accepted as the machine's. That is a denial of service, which a hostile
relay can already cause. What the harness lacks is conformance and a clear failure.

## The question

`CNF-87` and twr-ggw.3's matrix test the **relay** side of `WIR-8`. Does `WIR-8` also bind the
client? A browser cannot close with 1002 at all: `WebSocket.close()` accepts only 1000 or
3000–4999.
- **If it binds the client:** the harness must end the attempt on a text frame after OK, and the
  wire must say what a browser closes with.
- **If it does not:** paid-tcp-relay should say so.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The question above is answered upstream (paid-tcp-relay), at a pin this repository adopts.
- [ ] If the client is bound: the harness ends the attempt on a text frame after OK and does not
  pass its bytes to SSH. A tracer case shows it, with the relay fixture made to send such a
  frame.

title: paid-tcp-relay's WIR-8 at 844e834 is silent on a text frame between an accepted AUTH and OK
description:
## The gap

paid-tcp-relay's `WIR-8` at `844e834` says: "A text frame after `OK`, or a binary frame before it,
MUST close the connection with code 1002." It says nothing of a **text** frame the client sends
after its AUTH has been accepted but before OK. `WIR-5` says the client answers the challenge
with "one text frame, the AUTH", and `WIR-6`/`WIR-7` cover only that frame.

The relay fixture (twr-ggw.3, commit a0855f7, `tracer/src/fixtures.rs`) logs such a frame and
otherwise ignores it. A relay could equally close, with 1002 or 1008. twr-ggw.26 runs the
handshake test set against the publisher's relay, so a relay and the fixture could each pass
while disagreeing here.

## The question for paid-tcp-relay

What must a relay do with a text frame received after an accepted AUTH and before OK: ignore it,
or close the connection, and with which code?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] paid-tcp-relay answers the question, at a commit this repository adopts.
- [ ] The relay fixture follows the answer, and the relay matrix (`tracer/src/matrix.rs`) has a
  case that fails when it does not.

title: The CNF-13 source scan does not see a key held in a union or under a renamed import
description:
## The gap

twr-ggw.4 added `CNF-13`'s source scan (`src/credential.rs`, the tests module). It reads every
file under `src/` with `syn` and fails on a type that holds key material by its field types but
implements no `Credential`, so no `SEC-5` row. Two forms of key-holding type pass it unseen:

- **A union.** `visit_item_union` counts the union's name for the ambiguity rule, but always
  records it as holding no key. `union U { k: [u8; 32] }` in `src/` leaves the scan green.
- **A key type under another name.** Key types are matched by the last path segment
  (`SigningKey`, `SecretKey`, `PrivateKey`, …). `use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey as Sk;
  struct A(Sk);` leaves the scan green.

Neither form exists in `src/` today, so nothing is missed now. The scan is documented as a
guardrail, not a proof: it already cannot see a key carried in a `String` or a `Vec<u8>`. But the
module doc, the README and the scan's own doc say it fails on "a type that holds key material by
its field types". A union is such a type, and a renamed import is such a field type.

## The question

Should the guardrail cover these two forms, or should its documentation name them as outside it,
as it names `String` and `Vec<u8>`?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Either the scan reports a union holding key material, and a key type imported under another
  name, each shown by the planted-text test; or the scan's doc and the README name both forms as
  unseen.
close_reason: done

comments.author: user
comments.text: Closed by 71d8727, the criterion's second branch: the scan's doc on Scan and the README passage name a union's fields and a key type imported under another name as unseen, beside String and Vec<u8>; the module doc's claim is qualified to the scan's limits. No scan behaviour changed. The branch was settled by Consultation (all four advisers for documentation over extending the scan): neither form exists in src/, and resolving renamed imports needs a cross-file alias pass the guardrail does not justify. Gates: fmt, clippy, test, cors-probe, check-install-disks pass; --baseline fails as required.

title: The seed-backup ceremony STA-23 names has no owning ticket, and the store's seed is shown nowhere
description:
## What to build
Build the generated-seed backup ceremony inside the harness worker, outside every session. The allocation core and Store::seed_backup already journal completions; this ticket supplies their checked operator act and integrated refusal/display paths. A generated seed without its own durable record owes the ceremony at create, creation-finishing unlock and Replace. Imported seeds owe none and never allocate.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Stop dispatch, end session workers and close channels before showing all twelve words; display nowhere else. Hide all words while answering, and never pass them to a session, journal plaintext or log [STA-23, SEC-5 rows 15, 18, CNF-82].
- [ ] Full re-entry imports all twelve words and must produce the same seed id. A mismatch returns to the display. Alternatively an explicit skip completes the check. No partial re-entry or acknowledgement completes it [STA-23, CNF-82].
- [ ] Append the completion full_reentry or skipped for that seed id before applying it, using the store; report which occurred and call neither verified. A failed append leaves no completion [STA-3, STA-23, SEC-2, CNF-44, CNF-82].
- [ ] Create, unlock finishing interrupted creation, and Replace's fresh seed each owe the ceremony while the record is absent. Close the tab, hide the page and kill the worker before completion; next unlock still owes it. A failed completion append remains owed. Imported sheet and store-backup seeds owe no new ceremony [STA-23, CNF-82].
- [ ] Re-display requires the local passphrase again, stops sessions/channels and uses the same full ceremony, including hiding while answering. No other display exists [STA-23, SEC-5 rows 15, 18, CNF-82].
- [ ] In the integrated harness, refuse every allocating operation in all three families until a generated seed has its own durable record, across restart and during Replace's machine/pass allocations; generating the fresh seed itself is never gated. Show the operator why. Full re-entry and skip each admit after their durable append; inject a failed append and confirm allocation still refuses [STA-22b, STA-23, CNF-72].
- [ ] Inspect UI/worker messages, persisted bytes and worker/session inputs for forbidden custody; test each criterion on the integrated harness, including the distinction between full re-entry and skip [CNF-44, CNF-72, CNF-82, SEC-2].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.5 — existing encrypted store and lock lifecycle
- twr-ggw.72 — completion journal and allocation gate at the new pin

## Spec
STA-3, STA-22b, STA-23, SEC-2, SEC-5, CNF-44, CNF-72, CNF-82, ADR-0047, STA-22

## As filed (gap and question)

Kept verbatim as filed, at spec `ee133d0`: its quotations are that pin's, and its checkboxes are not live. The criteria above, at `8869ade`, supersede everything in this section.

## The gap

twr-ggw.5 (commit 37e8161) creates the local store with a seed generated inside the harness
worker, and keeps its mnemonic in the store's first, encrypted record. Nothing displays it: spec
`STA-23` says "The mnemonic may be displayed only in the dedicated seed-backup ceremony, outside
session/model context", and no ticket under this epic builds that ceremony. A search of every
ticket's title and description for "seed-backup", "seed backup" and "backup ceremony" finds none.

Until one exists, an operator who creates a store holds a seed they have never seen. `STA-22`
says the seed is "backed up by the operator the way this audience already backs up seeds", and
`SEC-5` row 15 places it "in the operator's head or seed backup". A lost store or a forgotten
local passphrase then loses the seed for good, and every key derived from it. That costs nothing
today, because nothing derives a machine's key from the seed yet. It costs every maintained
machine once binding (twr-ggw.11) and allocation (twr-ggw.6) use the seed.

The specification names the ceremony and says nothing else about it: not when it runs, not
whether setup waits for a confirmed backup, and not whether the operator must prove the backup,
for example by re-entering words.

## The question

Which ticket owns the seed-backup ceremony, and does the specification need to say more about it
before it is built, such as when it runs and what completes it?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A ticket owns the seed-backup ceremony, and it is ordered before the first ticket that
  derives a key the operator relies on from the seed.
- [ ] Any question the specification leaves open about the ceremony is taken to the specification
  repository first.

Separately every imported seed restores but never allocates, and a bare seed with no sheet/backup is refused. title: An imported seed must not allocate after a restart or an interrupted import, and Replace must take a fresh seed
description:
## The gap

twr-ggw.6 (commit 22a6dde) puts `STA-22b`'s restriction in the allocation core, and nowhere
else. A restore is an ordinary core event, and the restriction is part of the core's state. The
store replays a restore record of its own seed. But no store method writes one, and no store can
yet be created from an imported seed: that durable import path is twr-ggw.27's. `STA-22b` says
"a seed imported after loss of the canonical journal may restore listed identities but MUST NOT
allocate new ones", and "This restriction also applies to an imported local-store backup".

twr-ggw.27's criterion reads "A stale sheet or an imported store cannot allocate under the
restored seed". Four behaviours that criterion does not pin, each of which can reissue or lose an
identity:

1. **A restart.** The restriction holds only if it is journaled. A test that allocates once,
   in the same worker, passes even when the restriction lives only in memory. Lock, reload, page
   hide and a killed worker each restart the worker and replay the journal (twr-ggw.5). So the
   check must restart the worker and replay before it tries to allocate.
2. **An interrupted import.** Replay builds an unrestricted, fresh-seed allocation state from
   record 0's seed (`src/store.rs`, `Metadata::new(seed.id())`). And unlocking an envelope with no
   record finishes creation by generating a new seed (`Store::finish_creation`). Two failures
   follow:
   - An import that commits the imported seed's record and dies before the record carrying the
     restriction leaves a store that allocates under the imported seed.
   - An import that dies after the envelope falls through to a freshly generated seed.

   Each must reopen refused or incomplete, never as a store that allocates.
3. **Where a restore record may sit.** Replay applies a restore record of the store's own seed at
   any position. That replaces the entries and counters with the export's, so identities the
   journal recorded after that export vanish from the metadata. Allocation is barred until a
   Replace, so none is reissued under that seed. But a later sheet export would omit them.
4. **Replace's freshness.** The core refuses a Replace only to the current seed or to one an
   entry names. After a restore drops a later seed's entries, a Replace back to that seed is
   accepted and reissues its identities. `STA-17`'s Replace says "generate a **new seed**", so
   twr-ggw.29 must pass a freshly generated one, and nothing may rely on the core's guard as a
   freshness check.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The import path journals the restriction. After a worker restart and replay, allocation is
  refused in every family, under a test that restarts the worker [STA-22b].
- [ ] An import killed at each storage operation reopens refused or incomplete. It never reopens
  as a store that allocates, and never falls through to a freshly generated seed [STA-22b].
- [ ] Replay refuses a restore record anywhere the import path does not put it, unless the owner
  decides otherwise.
- [ ] Replace passes a freshly generated seed to the core, and a test shows that a Replace to a
  seed used before cannot reissue an identity [STA-17, STA-22b].
close_reason: Folded into twr-ggw.27 and twr-ggw.29

comments.text: Triage 2026-10-15: no spec gap (STA-22b and STA-17 already state each rule). Folded into twr-ggw.27 (criteria 1-3, AC3 taking the default: replay refuses a misplaced restore record) and twr-ggw.29 (criterion 4).

title: Allocation: an index is journaled before use and never reused
description:
## What to build
Per-family monotonic counters with consumed tombstones: an index is reserved durably before any external effect, and a reservation that produced no machine stays consumed. The journal refuses a machine at a recorded index, and a seed imported without its journal allocates nothing. The allocation core runs the companion comparison against the allocation witness file.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Deriving twice from the same seed and index gives identical keys, and the journal refuses to create a machine at a recorded index [CNF-72, STA-22].
- [ ] A reservation is journaled before any external effect, and a tombstoned index is never issued again [STA-22b].
- [ ] A seed imported after loss of the canonical journal restores the listed identities and allocates no new one [STA-22b].
- [ ] The allocation core passes the companion comparison against the allocation witness file at the spec pin, and CNF-3's three breaks each turn it red, naming the trace; the breaks are made once by hand and recorded here [CNF-3, ADR-0032].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.5 — The local store: unlock, append before apply, lock

## Spec
STA-22, STA-22b, ADR-0032, CNF-3, CNF-72
close_reason: Done in 22a6dde; Panel and Manager accepted Round 2

comments.author: user
comments.text:
Done in 22a6dde (feat: journal each allocation before use and never reuse an index). It took two Rounds, and every reviewer on the four-reviewer Panel accepted Round 2.

**What was built:**
- **The allocation core**, `src/allocation.rs`. It is pure and built on every target.
  - It holds STA-22b's allocation metadata, with a monotonic counter per family: machines, passes and handoffs.
  - Failed and destroyed entries are tombstones. They are never revived, and their index is never reissued.
  - No index past 2^31-1 is issued, and the counters never wrap.
  - Restore is an ordinary core event. It refuses allocation in every family until a Replace.
- **Journaling in the local store.**
  - Store::allocate takes no index. The reservation is appended, applied once committed, and only then returned (STA-3).
  - Replay applies each record through the same core. It fails closed on a recorded or skipped index, an unknown version, an allocation under the restriction, an inapplicable observation, a replace record, or a restore of another seed's metadata (CNF-72).

**Criteria:**
- **AC1, CNF-72 and STA-22.** The same keys re-derive after a reopen, and the journal refuses a machine at a recorded index, through the API and at replay.
- **AC2, STA-22b.** The commit lands before the identity is returned. A failed append, a move that lands and then reports failure, a kill after the commit, and tombstones across a reopen are each tested.
- **AC3, STA-22b.** The seed's mnemonic is imported after the store is discarded and the core's export is restored. The listed identities and their keys come back, and allocation is refused in all three families until a Replace with a fresh seed. The same refusal holds through a journaled restore record, after replay.
- **AC4, CNF-3 and ADR-0032.** The comparison reads spec/docs/design/allocation-witnesses-v1.json from the pinned tree at run time. Its record:
  - file: spec/docs/design/allocation-witnesses-v1.json; schema 1, module allocation;
  - bound: 3 events over an alphabet of 7;
  - compared: 6 witnesses and 400 enumerated traces, every step;
  - pair: TauWeb.Allocation.stale_sheet_refused matched, and TauWeb.Allocation.stale_sheet_admitted differed at step 7, the negative control;
  - spec commit: 1cc84987d76a5e9237e9e8a09287dc5e9e4c5ac4;
  - implementation revision: 22a6dde.

  The comparison also checks that the enumeration is complete for its bound, that every enumerated trace starts from the initial journal, and that the pair names itself both ways. Anything unknown fails, naming its trace.

**CNF-3's three breaks, made once by hand on 2026-10-12.** The comparison test's path was edited temporarily to a scratch copy outside spec/, since build.rs refuses a dirty spec/. It was green against the unmodified copy first.
1. **An outcome flipped**: TauWeb.Allocation.successful_trace, step 1, admitted changed to refused. Red: "TauWeb.Allocation.successful_trace, step 1 (allocate): allocation: expected refused, actual admitted".
2. **The file missing, then empty.** Red both times, naming the path:
   - "…/allocation-witnesses-v1.json: No such file or directory (os error 2)";
   - "…: not a JSON document: EOF while parsing a value at line 1 column 0".
3. **Unrecognised input.** Red both times, naming the trace:
   - enumeration[1]'s event kind changed to "reallocate": "enumeration[1], step 1: event: unknown variant `reallocate`";
   - its outcome changed to "granted": "enumeration[1], step 1: unknown variant `granted`".

Both the copy and the path edit were restored, confirmed with cmp, and the test went green again. The same breaks stay as permanent unit tests on the comparator, alongside a truncated enumeration, an unknown member, a pair missing its admitted side, and an enumerated trace (empty, or with steps) that starts away from the initial journal. README "The gates" records the by-hand breaks too.

**Mutation proofs.** Each was made by hand and turned its named tests red, and each restore was confirmed with cmp:
- Round 1: allocation under the restriction; a failed index reissued; a failed entry revived; the exhaustion check removed; apply before commit; replay accepting a recorded identity; Replace leaving the restriction set.
- Round 2: the start check removed. Two reviewers reproduced this one independently.

**Consultation (pick).** The question was whether AC3 is realised on the core only, or through a store import path now. It settled on the core only, 3–1: three advisers for it, one for the store path. Durable import stays with twr-ggw.27. The record is in the Run's brief.

**Notes for later tickets:**
- **The tracer reader's needle check.** seed_secrets in tracer/src/reader.rs lists the seed identifier as a needle, and the reader test asserts that no decrypted record after record 0 holds one. An allocation record carries the seed identifier inside the encryption, where credential format v1 puts it. So the first ticket that writes allocation records into a store the reader reads will see that assertion go red, loudly. That ticket should exempt the identifier inside allocation records.
- **A README sentence lost its antecedent (cosmetic).** In "The gates", the tracer sentence "broken the same way" now follows the comparison breaks rather than the 2026-09-21 general-form break.

**Follow-up:** twr-ggw.59 (needs-triage). An imported seed must keep the restriction across a restart and an interrupted import, a restore record's position needs deciding, and Replace must take a fresh seed.

title: Bump the spec pin to ee133d0 (STA-24's disposition rule)
description:
## What to build
Move the spec pin from 1cc8498 to the spec's main, ee133d0 ("feat(spec): STA-24 states a
disposition's reach, lapse, naming and replay (#18)"), so twr-ggw.7 builds against the disposition
rule it waited on. Between the two pins:

- STA-24 and STA-20b state a standing disposition's reach (what its calls barred; a destructive
  continuation also stops the model's box-plane commands, harness jobs it requests included;
  reads and the inference request are never restricted), where it ends (the continuation's

title: No ticket lets the operator record a disposition or shows unresolved calls and dispositions on screen
description:
## What
twr-ggw.7 (commit 761a5b6) records dispositions through `Store::dispose`, an operator act with no
caller in the product: no screen lets the operator choose one, and no page message reaches it.
The store returns what `STA-24` says the operator is shown, and `store_state` exposes it. But the

`STA-24` (spec `ee133d0`, `03-state-and-recovery.md`) asks for each of these:
- "the unresolved call is shown in its place: to the model as the tool result, to the operator on
  the screen" (line 193);
- a refused disposition: "the operator is shown that it was refused, the record that settled the

title: The operator's disposition act, and unresolved calls and dispositions on screen
description:
## What to build
The operator records a disposition by an act on the screen, outside any model path. For one resource, the operator names some or all of its unresolved calls (or, to replace the standing disposition, the calls it disposed), chooses one of the four continuations, and records the uncertainty accepted. The harness worker records it through the store's disposition test (`Store::dispose`, twr-ggw.7), and the screen shows what happened. The screen shows each resource's unresolved calls; its standing disposition and that disposition's continuation; every refused disposition, with what settled the call and what is unresolved now; what a replacement replaced; every disposition refused at replay; evidence that arrived after a disposition; and each request the barrier refused, with the call that refused it. twr-ggw.8 supplies the typed operations and the reports its criteria make for the operator's screen; pairing a refused request with the unresolved call that refused it is this ticket's, in the harness as on the screen.

Not this ticket's: dispatching a continuation (the abandonment flow is twr-ggw.31's, the stop that stands in for a destroy twr-ggw.40's, the reinstall twr-ggw.45's, the reset into rescue twr-i6k.3's); the model's tool result when a request is refused (twr-ggw.67); ARC-22's opening screen (twr-ggw.31); an unresolved inference request shown as unaccounted spend (twr-ggw.17); a sibling entry's approval card (twr-ggw.21); the screen's statement before a destructive choice under an untyped vendor scope (CNF-105, stage 2).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A disposition is recorded only by the operator's act on the screen: "Neither a timer nor the model supplies one", and of a replacement, "Neither a timer nor the model replaces one". Implementation reading: no model tool, harness job or timer reaches the act, and a test fails if any path other than the operator's act records a disposition [STA-24].
- [ ] The act names one resource; at least one call, each unresolved on that resource or, for a replacement, disposed by the standing disposition; one of the four continuations, "a destructive reinstall (`STG-20`), abandonment (`ARC-21`), continuing as if done, continuing as if not done"; and "the uncertainty accepted". The store's test decides it, and an accepted disposition is durably appended before it is applied [STA-24, STA-3].
- [ ] Each unresolved call is shown on the screen with its resource and what was requested (the box-plane command, or the typed operation's approved facts), as unresolved: it "is not reported as failed", and it is never shown as pending, in flight, failed or timed out [STA-8, CNF-29, CONTEXT.md "Unresolved"].
- [ ] A refused request shows the unresolved call on screen; for a request made by a session return that call as the tool result through twr-ggw.67. A disposition refusal shows the standing disposition and continuation [STA-24].
- [ ] Each resource's standing disposition is shown with the calls it disposed, its continuation and the uncertainty accepted, and each disposed call's outcome is shown as unknown: "it is never written as success, failure, zero spend or non-execution" [STA-24].
- [ ] Under either continuation that continues, the screen shows the operator's recorded assumption, continuing as if done or continuing as if not done, "which is shown and never written as success, failure, zero spend or non-execution" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] A disposition that names no call, names a call already settled (by a terminal record, or by a disposition other than the standing one, whose calls only a replacement may name: "a new disposition may name the calls the standing one disposed"), or names a call on another resource records nothing, and the screen shows "that it was refused, the record that settled the call if one did, and what is unresolved now" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] After a disposition naming some of several unresolved calls, the screen shows the named calls under it and the others still unresolved: "the unnamed ones stay unresolved and keep their barrier" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] After a replacement, "the operator is shown what it replaces", and the screen shows the replacement's continuation as the one in force; with a destructive reinstall replaced by abandonment, abandonment is shown in force [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] Once the continuation is dispatched, with its intent durably appended, the screen no longer shows the disposition as standing and shows that call instead: the disposition "stands until its continuation is dispatched or the operator replaces it", and "from then on that call's own barrier governs" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] A disposition in a replayed journal that the test refuses is shown as refused, and no call is shown as disposed by it: "it ends no call and restricts nothing, every call it named that is unresolved stays unresolved and keeps its barrier, and the operator is shown the record" [CNF-110, STA-24, STA-7].
- [ ] Evidence about a disposed call that arrives after its disposition is shown beside that call, which stays shown as disposed under the standing disposition: it "is journaled and shown: it neither reopens the call nor removes the disposition" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] Nothing the screen receives for the act or the display carries key material, the seed or a credential the harness holds; the UI "never receives the unwrapped data key" [STA-23, SEC-5].
- [ ] Each criterion above has a test that fails when the act or the screen breaks it.

- [ ] List each call a replacement drops; it stays settled with unknown outcome under the replaced record and can never be named again. When replacing reinstall with a continuing choice, say commands resume and resets meet remaining checks. With no standing approval say the reinstall is cancelled (under an untyped vendor scope say the hold is released). With approvals standing require keep or explicit withdrawal for each, as separate journal acts through twr-i6k.10. On the dedicated path show the unknown-activation reset warning and offer retry the activation, keep the reinstall; test CNF-110's dedicated screen cases there [STA-24, STG-20, CNF-110].

- [ ] A disposition releases only the named command's STA-20 unresolved-command hold; unnamed unresolved commands keep theirs. A destructive continuation still refuses every box-plane job. Show STA-20's collection wait and operator stop without claiming it settled a call, and leave a stopped harness flow for explicit operator resumption [STA-20, STA-24, CNF-40, CNF-110].

- twr-ggw.8 — Typed operations on a fixture adapter, behind the unresolved barrier

## What to build

unresolved, the model's tool result carries that unresolved call. `STA-24` says "The request is

title: STA-20's hold: an unresolved box-plane command holds its machine
description:
## What to build
`STA-20`'s hold, decided at spec d029ebd (ADR-0048): "While a box-plane command to a machine is unresolved (`STA-8`), the harness worker MUST NOT dispatch another box-plane command to that machine, whatever its call id, tool, requester or session; a read through `exec` is a command, and a job the harness composes is held too." `STA-24` now says "at most one box-plane command is unresolved (`STA-20`'s hold)".

Today the dispatch check refuses a box-plane command only under a standing destructive disposition, so a second command, or an explicit reissue of the same bytes, to a machine with an unresolved call is admitted and run. This ticket puts the hold into that check and gives a held request what `STA-20` says it gets, on the path that dispatches box-plane commands today (`run_command`) and the collection beside it (`collect_jobs`).

The rule, quoted whole from `STA-20` at d029ebd:
- "Collecting a job record is not held, and other machines are unaffected."
- "Only a terminal record releases the hold: a finished record of any command but `delivery_reboot`, `delivery_reboot`'s boot change (`ARC-43`), or a disposition, which `STA-24` says "is a terminal record of its own kind"; otherwise an ended, missing or incomplete record does not, and no timeout does."
- "The dispatch check carries the rule and the single writer serializes it with the intent's append, so two requests cannot both pass."
- "A held request is not run and records no intent."
- "The harness collects the calls holding it, waiting while a command's own process or its runner is alive; a call whose own dispatch is still awaiting its record is not collected separately, the held request waits on that same result."
- "The wait does not hold the writer, is shown to the operator and may be stopped; stopping settles nothing, and a machine that cannot be reached is answered at once."
- `STA-24`: "The disposition releases the named command's hold; unnamed unresolved commands retain theirs."

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The dispatch check refuses a box-plane command to a machine that has an unresolved box-plane command, before any contact and again atomically with the intent's append, whatever the command's bytes (a read included, and the same bytes as the holding call included); the refused request runs nothing and records no intent [STA-20, STA-24, CNF-40].
- [ ] Two requests to one machine made together: exactly one records an intent and runs; the other is held [STA-20, STA-1, CNF-40 (two requests made together)].
- [ ] An ended, missing or incomplete job record keeps the machine held, and so does an unread call; a finished record releases it; so does a disposition naming the holding call with a continuation that continues; a call disposed with a destructive continuation still has every box-plane job to that machine refused; no timer releases anything [STA-20, STA-24, CNF-40, CNF-55].
- [ ] Collection is never held, and a command to another machine is unaffected by this machine's hold [STA-20, CNF-40].
- [ ] A held request collects the calls holding it, waiting while the command's own process or its runner is alive, then answers held without running; it never dispatches its own command afterwards, even when collection finished the holding call (the caller asks again). A machine that cannot be reached is answered at once [STA-20, CNF-40].
- [ ] A collection started while the holding call's own `run_command` still awaits that call's record does not read or append that call separately: the held request waits on that same result, and the call gets exactly one result. This absorbs twr-ggw.14's former criterion found in the twr-ggw.12 review [STA-20, STA-1, CNF-40 (collection started while the earlier call's own dispatch awaits its record)].

title: Box-plane commands go through the journal and survive a killed worker
description:
## What to build
The tracer's command now passes the dispatch core: an intent record before send and a terminal record after. An intent with no terminal record is unresolved, is never retried automatically, and ends only on evidence or on a disposition naming one continuation. A killed worker restarts locked, and replay classifies incomplete calls, cancels those never dispatched and surfaces the rest without resuming them.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each box-plane command is recorded before transmission [CNF-30, ARC-8, STA-4].
- [ ] A command interrupted between its intent and its terminal record is unresolved: not retried, not reported as failed, and cleared by no timer [CNF-29 (box-plane case), STA-8].
- [ ] A disposition permits only the continuation it names and keeps the outcome unknown [STA-24].
- [ ] After a killed worker, replay cancels the intents never dispatched and surfaces the uncertain ones without resuming them [CNF-39, STA-7].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.5 — The local store: unlock, append before apply, lock

## Spec
STA-3, STA-4, STA-6, STA-7, STA-8, STA-24, ARC-8, CNF-29, CNF-30, CNF-39

title: Each collection appends another identical observation for a call already ended or missing
description:
## What
`Dispatch::collectable` (src/dispatch.rs) keeps every unresolved call with a job identity eligible
for collection. Each `collect_jobs` therefore reads again a call whose record already showed it
ended (a changed boot, or its process gone with no exit code) or missing, and appends another
`job_observation` identical to the last. The journal and `store_state`'s `jobs` grow on every
collection with nothing new: in a tracer run one missing call was appended at three records, one
ended call at three more.

An ended record from an old boot can never change. A missing one is "unresolved, never proof of
death" (`STA-20`), so it may be read again; that is no reason to journal the same observation each
time.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A collection journals a job observation for a call only when it differs from the latest one
already journaled for that call; the collection still reports what it read [STA-20, STA-3].
- [ ] Two collections over an unchanged ended call and an unchanged missing call journal one
observation each, and `store_state`'s `jobs` does not grow on the second [STA-20].
- [ ] A read that changes (a missing record now present, a running job now ended) is journaled
[STA-20, STA-3].
- [ ] The tests fail when the comparison with the latest observation is removed.

## Spec
STA-20, STA-3

title: twr-ggw.12 review: oversized commands never launch; a fast command can lose its record
description:
## What
The review of twr-ggw.12 (commits 46b72f0, 626af02) found two defects in the job launch, each
verified against the code:

1. **A command over about 25 KB can never launch.** `src/jobs.rs` `octal()` writes each command byte
   as 5 characters and the launch adds about 6 KB of fixed text; sshd runs the launch as one
   `$SHELL -c` argument, and Linux caps one argument at 131072 bytes ("Argument list too long",
   exit 126). The intent is journaled, the exec fails, no job directory exists, and every later
   collection reads `missing`: the call stays unresolved until a disposition.
2. **A fast command can lose its record at startup.** `src/jobs/runner.sh`'s wait loop runs
   `kill -0 "$command_pid" || exit 1` after `[ ! -f "$d/pid" ]` and never tests the file again; bash
   reaps a finished child at once, so a command that ends in that gap leaves `pid` without `ready`
   or `exit`, and collection reads `incomplete` forever although the command ran.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A command whose composed launch would exceed the argument limit is refused before its intent
  is appended, with a reason the operator and the model see; a test shows the refusal and that
  nothing is journaled. The bound is a named constant with its derivation [STA-20, CNF-28].
- [ ] The runner's start loop tests for the `pid` file again after `kill -0` fails, and a test (a
  scratch runner that widens the gap) shows a command that ends in the gap still records `ready` and
  its exit status [STA-20, CNF-40].
- [ ] The same re-test is applied wherever the launch loop has the pattern (`src/jobs.rs`'s
  `ready` wait), or the ticket records why it is safe there.

## Spec
STA-20, CNF-28, CNF-40
close_reason: Refuses oversized launches and keeps fast job records, accepted after Round 1; see the closing comment.

title: Bump the spec pin to 8869ade, and bring the open tickets to it
description:
## What to build
Move the spec pin from ee133d0 to the spec's main, 8869ade ("feat(spec): the grill of
2026-10-15/17 — dispositions, rescue, recovery and worker policy (#20)"), keep every gate green,
and bring every open ticket to the pinned text. Between the two pins: ADR-0045, ADR-0046 and
ADR-0047 and `CNF-111` are new; `docs/design/allocation-witnesses-v1.json` is replaced by
`allocation-witnesses-v2.json`, `dispatch-witnesses-v2.json` by `dispatch-witnesses-v5.json`
(new `approve_reinstall` and `withdraw_reinstall` events, new `start` records) and
`pins-witnesses-v4.json` by `pins-witnesses-v5.json`; the delivery declaration is version 2
(`services[].scope`, version 1 refused); the credential format's sheet payload gains
`seed_backup`; `docs/briefs/01-install.md` and the three tenant profiles changed. `bundle/` is
unchanged.

### The code the pin forces, owned here
`src/allocation/comparison.rs` reads `allocation-witnesses-v1.json`, which is gone at the pin.
Its successor adds a `seed_backup` journal member, a `seed_backup` event and a second guard,
`backupRecorded`, and its `backup_missing_refused` witness expects an allocation refused with no
ceremony record. So this ticket moves the comparison to v2 and gives the allocation core what the
file forces: the seed's ceremony record in `Metadata`, the event that records it, and `issue`
refusing every family under a generated seed without it (`STA-22b`: "Under a generated seed,
allocation in every family — machines, relay passes and handoffs — MUST be refused until that
seed id has the journaled ceremony record of `STA-23`"), with Restore and Replace doing to the
record what the witness file's journal projection says. Store tests that allocate record the
ceremony first; nothing bypasses the gate. The ceremony itself (display, all-or-zero re-entry,
the skip, owed again after an interruption, re-display, the operator-facing refusal, and
`CNF-82`'s and `CNF-72`'s integrated cases) stays twr-ggw.58's.

### The tickets
Rewrite a criterion (current description plus the edit, through `br update --description-file`)
where the ticket's duty changed, comment where only its context changed. In particular:
- **Witness partitions.** twr-ggw.8's and twr-i6k.3's dispatch criteria move to
  `dispatch-witnesses-v5.json`, and twr-ggw.43's and twr-i6k.3's pins criteria to
  `pins-witnesses-v5.json`. Same rule as before: the dedicated ticket takes the traces that
  consult a rescue rule, now including the reinstall approval and withdrawal events and `start`
  records. twr-ggw.43's bucket "pending tw-vk9" is gone (the spec moved attest admission to the

  ready-for-agent, blocking twr-ggw.8, .10, .11 and .29. Worker self-check and the host's
  policy header (`ARC-32`, `ARC-33`, `CNF-111`): twr-ggw.54, ready-for-agent. Every import
  restores but never allocates, and a bare seed is refused (`STA-22b`, `CNF-84`): twr-ggw.27.
  The 16-byte minimum (`SEC-5`): twr-ggw.38 (twr-ggw.23 keeps pointing to it). The delivery
  reboot the operator opts into, and the "enabled, restart not demonstrated" label (`ARC-43`,
  `CNF-53`): twr-ggw.36, with the re-entry offer twr-ggw.50's. The service-name grammar and
  `scope`: the ticket that issues unit-state reads, and the declaration's version 2 where
  declarations are proposed (twr-ggw.15). The abandonment flow's authorization (`SEC-4`) and the
  refusal of a session destroy under a standing abandonment (`STA-24`): twr-ggw.31 and
  twr-ggw.40. The installation id shown to the model (`STG-20`, `ARC-7`), Replace's relabel
  (`STA-17`) and the operator's withdrawal of a reinstall approval (`STG-20`): one new ticket

- **Unpark.** twr-ggw.8, .54 and .58 become ready-for-agent where the pinned text now specifies

[CNF-1, ADR-0031].
- [ ] The format, lint and test gates pass, run unpiped, at the declared strictness, and the CORS
probe runs from the pinned tree [CNF-2, CNF-4].

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""One decision list per comparison, measured at both pins, with pair checks."""
import collections
import json
from pathlib import Path
BASE=Path('/var/tmp/tau-web-rust-8869ade')

def dispatch(trace, new=True):
    start=trace['start']
    dispositions=list(start['dispositions'])
    if start['reset_offer'] or (new and any(start[k] for k in
        ('reinstall_approvals','reinstall_withdrawals','prerequisite_records'))):
        return 'dedicated'
    for step in trace['steps']:
        event=step['event']; kind=event['kind']
        if kind=='reset_prereqs' or (new and kind in ('approve_reinstall','withdraw_reinstall')):
            return 'dedicated'
        if kind in ('request','read'):
            if event['operation'] in ('activate','register_key'):
                return 'dedicated'
            if kind=='request' and event['operation']=='reset' and any(
                d['continuation']=='destructive_reinstall' for d in dispositions):
                return 'dedicated'
        if kind=='dispose': dispositions.append(event)
    return 'stage1'

def pins(trace, new=True):
    steps=trace['steps']; kinds={s['event']['kind'] for s in steps}
    if not new:
        if 'attest' in kinds: return 'attest'
        if kinds & {'reset','rescue_last'}: return 'dedicated'
        return 'stage1'
    if kinds & {'reset','rescue_last'}:
        return 'attest' if 'attest' in kinds else 'dedicated'
    sources=[n for n,s in enumerate(steps) if s['event']['kind'] in ('attest','ready_to_reset')]
    if not sources: return 'stage1'
    if sources==list(range(len(sources))) and all(steps[n]['pinned'] for n in sources) and any(
        s['event']['kind']=='published' for s in steps[len(sources):]):
        return 'stage1'
    if 'attest' in kinds: return 'attest'
    return 'dedicated'

def measure(doc, rule):
    result={}
    for group in ('witnesses','enumeration'):
        counts=collections.Counter(rule(t) for t in doc[group])
        assert sum(counts.values())==len(doc[group])
        result[group]=dict(sorted(counts.items()))
        by_name={d:t for t in doc[group] for d in t['declarations']}
        pairs=0
        for t in doc[group]:
            if 'pair' in t:
                other=by_name[t['pair']['with']]
                assert rule(t)==rule(other),(t['declarations'],other['declarations'])
                pairs+=1
        print(group, json.dumps(result[group],sort_keys=True), 'paired sides', pairs, 'no split')
    return result

def vocab(doc, owner):
    sets=collections.defaultdict(set)
    for group in ('witnesses','enumeration'):
        for t in doc[group]:
            if dispatch(t)!=owner: continue
            sets['start_members'].update(t['start'])
            for step in t['steps']:
                ev=step['event']; sets['kinds'].add(ev['kind'])
                for key in ('operation','continuation','source'):
                    if key in ev: sets[key].add(str(ev[key]))
                sets['outcome_members'].update(set(step)-{'event','knowledge'})
                sets['projection_members'].update(step['knowledge'])
                if 'refusal' in step:
                    sets['refusal_reasons'].add(step['refusal']['reason'])
    return {k:sorted(v) for k,v in sorted(sets.items())}

results={}
for rev,dname,pname in [('ee133d0','dispatch-witnesses-v2.json','pins-witnesses-v4.json'),
                        ('8869ade','dispatch-witnesses-v5.json','pins-witnesses-v5.json')]:
    docs=[json.loads((BASE/('spec-'+rev)/'docs/design'/n).read_text()) for n in (dname,pname)]
    for name,doc,rule in zip(('dispatch','pins'),docs,(dispatch,pins)):
        print(rev,name)
        result=measure(doc,lambda t:rule(t,rev=='8869ade'))
        results[rev+'-'+name]=result
    if rev=='ee133d0':
        assert results[rev+'-dispatch']=={'witnesses':{'stage1':24,'dedicated':17},'enumeration':{'stage1':227,'dedicated':173}}
        assert results[rev+'-pins']=={'witnesses':{'stage1':42,'dedicated':13,'attest':16},'enumeration':{'stage1':2955,'dedicated':3220,'attest':2246}}
    else:
        d,p=docs
        reused=[]
        for group in ('witnesses','enumeration'):
            for i,t in enumerate(d[group]):
                calls=[s['event']['call'] for s in t['steps'] if s['event']['kind']=='request']
                if len(calls)!=len(set(calls)): reused.append((group,i))
        assert not reused,reused
        print('dispatch repeated request call ids:',reused)
        for owner in ('stage1','dedicated'):
            results['vocabulary-'+owner]=vocab(d,owner)
            print('dispatch',owner,'vocabulary:',json.dumps(results['vocabulary-'+owner],sort_keys=True))
        for group in ('witnesses','enumeration'):
            mixed=sum(bool({'reset','rescue_last'} & {s['event']['kind'] for s in t['steps']}) and any(s['event']['kind']=='attest' for s in t['steps']) for t in p[group])
            seeded=collections.Counter()
            for t in p[group]:
                if pins(t)!='stage1':continue
                for kind in ('attest','ready_to_reset'):
                    if any(s['event']['kind']==kind for s in t['steps']):seeded[kind]+=1
            print('pins',group,'mixed rescue/attest:',mixed,'seeded:',dict(seeded))
        w=next(t for t in p['witnesses'] if 'TauWeb.Pins.unused_attest_after_reinstall_admitted' in t['declarations'])
        assert pins(w)=='attest'
        print('unused_attest_after_reinstall_admitted:',pins(w))
        for t in p['enumeration']:
            if [s['event']['kind'] for s in t['steps']]==['ready_to_reset','reinstall','connect']:
                assert pins(t)=='dedicated'
        print('ready_to_reset, reinstall, connect: dedicated')
(BASE/'partitions.json').write_text(json.dumps(results,indent=2)+'\n')
```

title: Running-at-delivery binds until the boot changes, and re-entry reads every declared unit
description:
## What to build
`ARC-43`'s decided rule for when a `running-at-delivery` service binds (spec d029ebd, ADR-0049), and the re-entry read of every declared service's unit. `OPN-14` now says "Re-entry reads every declared service's unit and reads enablement only for `enabled-survives-reboot` services (`ARC-43`, decided 2026-10-18, ADR-0049)."

The rule, quoted whole from `ARC-43`'s "When `running-at-delivery` binds":
- "Each check that finds the service running MUST journal the boot identity with that result."
- "Its lifecycle binds on that boot until the boot changes; a service never found running binds."
- "An amendment that newly declares a service `running-at-delivery` re-anchors it: from that amendment it counts as never found running, so it binds until a check finds it running."
- "Stopped on that boot is a lifecycle finding (`ARC-17`)."
- "Stopped after that boot changed, having been found running on it, raises no finding and MUST carry the note **"stopped since a restart, as approved"** wherever Delivered appears for that machine."
- "A boot change never clears a standing lifecycle finding; with that service's `running-at-delivery` promise unchanged, a re-check clears it only when it finds the service running."
- "An edit that leaves the promise as it was neither clears a standing finding nor turns a note into a finding."
- "In a session that places a secret, this note does not count for the post-placement demonstration (`ARC-17`): a stopped service is a lifecycle finding there."

twr-ggw.36 builds the unit-state reads and lifecycle findings at the delivery check, and twr-ggw.50 the enablement reads and reboot offer at re-entry; this ticket adds the boot anchor, the note and the re-entry unit read on top of them.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every delivery check and re-check that finds a `running-at-delivery` service running journals the boot identity with that result, before the result is shown [ARC-43, STA-3].
- [ ] On re-entry, every declared service's unit is read; enablement is read only for `enabled-survives-reboot` services [ARC-43, OPN-14, STG-9].
- [ ] Stopped on the boot it was last found running on, or never found running, is a lifecycle finding; stopped after that boot changed raises no finding and carries "stopped since a restart, as approved" wherever Delivered appears for that machine (delivery card and trust display) [ARC-43, ARC-17, CNF-53].
- [ ] A crash finding followed by a restart stays until a re-check finds the service running; a boot change never clears a standing lifecycle finding [ARC-43, CNF-53].
- [ ] A session that places a secret needs every `running-at-delivery` service running after its last placement; there the note does not count and a stopped service is a lifecycle finding [ARC-43, ARC-17, CNF-53].
- [ ] A journaled declaration amendment: withdrawing the promise and re-checking clears the finding; newly declaring or putting the promise back counts the service as never found running, so stopped is a finding, not the note, until a check finds it running; an edit that keeps the promise leaves a standing finding standing and a note a note [ARC-43, ARC-17, CNF-53].
- [ ] Each case above has a test on fixture observations that fails when the rule is broken, and the integrated harness exercises CNF-53's running-at-delivery cases, CNF-108's later-session case included [CNF-53, CNF-108].

## Not this ticket's
- The unit-state reads, service grammar and lifecycle findings at the delivery check: twr-ggw.36.
- Enablement reads and the reboot offer at re-entry: twr-ggw.50.
- The journaled declaration amendment itself, and a finding cleared by a re-check after one: twr-ggw.19.

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.36 — Service lifecycle findings
- twr-ggw.50 — Service lifecycle at re-entry: CNF-53 case (e)
- twr-ggw.35 — the pin carrying OPN-14's decision (closes with the d029ebd bump)

## Spec
ARC-43, ARC-17, OPN-14, STG-9, CNF-53, CNF-108, ADR-0049
