title: Bump the spec pin to d029ebd, and bring the open tickets to it
description:
## What to build
Move the spec pin from 8869ade to the spec's main, d029ebd ("fix(spec): a reinstall and the LNVPS stop end nothing for a placed secret (#23)", on top of df2d84a, "feat(spec): the machine hold, running-at-delivery and destructive stops (#22)"), keep every gate green, and bring every open ticket to the pinned text.

Between the two pins: ADR-0048 (an unresolved command holds its machine), ADR-0049 (running-at-delivery binds until the boot changes) and ADR-0050 (a destructive disposition stops every box-plane job) are new, and ADR-0022, ADR-0032, ADR-0041 and ADR-0044 are amended. `docs/design/dispatch-witnesses-v5.json` is replaced by `dispatch-witnesses-v6.json`: schema 6 adds the `commandHold` and `rebootBootChange` guards, the `delivery_reboot` operation, the `collect_reboot` event and the `reboot_results` projection (`docs/design/witness-file-v1.md`). The delivery declaration's `services` row gains one sentence. TASKS T35, T42 and T50 changed. The spec ids whose bodies changed, by `spec/tools/check_citations.py`'s `owners()`: ARC-17, ARC-1a, ARC-39, ARC-43, CNF-110, CNF-29, CNF-40, CNF-42, CNF-44, CNF-53, CNF-55, CNF-86, CNF-95, OPN-14, OPN-28, SEC-5, SEC-6, STA-17, STA-20, STA-20a, STA-20b, STA-24, STA-8, STG-21; none added or withdrawn. `bundle/`, `docs/tenants/`, `docs/briefs/`, `prototypes/`, `allocation-witnesses-v2.json`, `pins-witnesses-v5.json` and the credential format and vectors are unchanged.

### The code the pin forces, owned here
Measured before this ticket: in a scratch clone with only the pin moved to d029ebd, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` all exit 0 (101 + 4 + 47 tests). The crate reads no dispatch witness file; it reads `allocation-witnesses-v2.json` and the credential vectors, both unchanged. So this ticket changes no behaviour. It corrects what the repository says that the pinned text now contradicts:
- `src/dispatch.rs`'s module documentation says "Box-plane calls can be unresolved together." `STA-24` now says "at most one box-plane command is unresolved (`STA-20`'s hold)".
- The README says "There is no barrier between box-plane commands, including explicit reissues of the same bytes while another call is unresolved (`STA-24`'s box-plane carve-out)" and "A fresh `run_command` neither collects first nor waits on another job; the existing box-plane carve-out still applies." The carve-out is gone. State what the build does today and that it falls short of `STA-20`'s hold, which twr-ggw.69 builds; never describe today's admission as permitted by the pinned text.
- The README's pin, its stage-1 paragraph and every quotation and CNF label it carries match the pinned text. The "Stage 1: required" row's item list is unchanged, but item 53's and item 55's `delivery_reboot` cases now belong to the dedicated row, and item 95's cases (e) and (f) A/B output-release assertions (and case (e)'s copied-key assertions) to stage 2.

Building `STA-20`'s hold (twr-ggw.69), `delivery_reboot` or any other new behaviour is not this ticket's.

### The tickets
Rewrite a criterion (the current description plus the edit, through `br update --description-file`) where a ticket's duty changed; comment where only its context changed.

Already triaged on this branch, in commit 502a8d5: twr-ggw.69 (the hold's build ticket), twr-ggw.73 (running-at-delivery's build ticket), twr-ggw.14, .24 and .67 (the hold's model, successor-session and tool-result cases), and twr-ggw.35 and twr-tk3 (carried). Do not reopen those decisions; close twr-ggw.35 and twr-tk3 as carried once the pin commit lands.

In particular:
- **Dispatch witness partitions.** twr-ggw.8's and twr-i6k.3's dispatch criteria move to `dispatch-witnesses-v6.json`. Keep the rule that the dedicated ticket takes the traces that consult a rescue rule. Traces with a `delivery_reboot` request or a `collect_reboot` event, and that consult no rescue rule, go to the new `delivery_reboot` ticket below. Everything else stays twr-ggw.8's `stage1` bucket, which now holds `commandHold`'s traces, so twr-ggw.8 waits on twr-ggw.69. Each refused/admitted pair stays whole, and each guard's pair is a negative control.
- **`delivery_reboot` moves to the dedicated path.** File one ticket under twr-i6k for the harness's `delivery_reboot` job (`ARC-43`): the operator's yes journaled with its intent, its settlement by a collection reading a boot other than the record's own, the pending-check hold until the delivery check's verdict or the operator's journaled stop, the command in flight at the yes, the late new-boot record under a destructive disposition, and its share of `CNF-53`, `CNF-55` and `CNF-110` as the dedicated row lists them. Take those duties out of twr-ggw.36, which keeps LNVPS's typed-restart cases and the `exec` of the same reboot bytes, as the stage-1 row lists them.
- **A destructive disposition stops every box-plane job** (`STA-24`, ADR-0050), the harness's own jobs included: the tickets that compose `delivery_reboot`, `replace_root_label` (twr-i6k.9), Replace's key install and old-key removal (twr-ggw.29), `digest_secret` (twr-ggw.23) and the delivery check's harness-composed reads.
- **Each ticket that composes a harness job** (those above) carries `CNF-40`'s held-harness-job case for its job: `STA-20` says "A held harness job is not queued: the flow that needs it stays shown and composes it afresh once the hold lifts, a first issue and not a retry; after a stopped wait only the operator resumes that flow, and nothing left armed survives replay."
- **Replace under a hold** (`STA-17`): a machine under `STA-20`'s hold or a standing destructive disposition is shown as not yet migrated and keeps its old key, in twr-ggw.29 and twr-i6k.9; the relabel's re-read waits until `STA-20` and `STA-24` admit it.
- **The re-arm under a destructive disposition** (`ARC-1a`, `SEC-5`): the local paste card offered at once, a disposed digest that arms nothing, and the re-read restarted by one operator act, in twr-ggw.23, .25 and .28 as each one's scope reaches.
- **The LNVPS destroy** (`SEC-5` rows 12 and 23, T50): the vendor's confirmed deletion, not the stop, ends a placed secret's listing at LNVPS; twr-ggw.40, .23 and .25 as their scope reaches, and a comment on twr-ki8 (T50 now names the deletion contract).
- **Rescue** (`STA-20b`, `CNF-86`): the wait is `STA-20`'s hold, in twr-i6k.3 and twr-i6k.5.
- **`CNF-95`'s cases (e) and (f)**: their A/B assertions are stage 2's, in twr-ggw.23 and twr-ggw.52.
- **Every other open ticket** citing a changed id, ADR or task above (about fifty, the needs-info and external ones included): read the cited text at both pins and rewrite or comment as the change warrants; do not mirror spec-side beads (tw-i55, tw-pkn) into this tracker.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The spec pin is at d029ebd, and the build refuses a checked-out tree that differs from it [CNF-1, ADR-0031].
- [ ] The format, lint and test gates pass, run unpiped, and the CORS probe and the install-disk checks run from the pinned tree as CI runs them [CNF-2, CNF-4].
- [ ] No sentence in `src/` or the README says box-plane commands may be unresolved together or cites `STA-24`'s removed carve-out; the README names the new pin, and its quotations and CNF labels match the pinned text [STA-20, STA-24].
- [ ] twr-ggw.8's and twr-i6k.3's criteria, and the new `delivery_reboot` ticket's, name `dispatch-witnesses-v6.json` with counts computed by a script run against the pinned file and kept in the Run's record; the buckets sum to the file's totals [ADR-0032].
- [ ] The commit lists the changed spec ids, ADRs and tasks above, and every open ticket whose cited spec text changed is rewritten or commented.
- [ ] twr-ggw.35 and twr-tk3 are closed as carried by d029ebd.

## Spec

```python
    for step in t['steps']:
        e=step['event']; kind=e['kind']
        if kind in ('reset_prereqs','approve_reinstall','withdraw_reinstall'):
            return True
        if kind in ('request','read'):
            if e['operation'] in ('activate','register_key'): return True
            if kind=='request' and e['operation']=='reset' and any(
                    d['continuation']=='destructive_reinstall' for d in dispositions):
                return True
        if kind=='dispose': dispositions.append(e)
    return False

def reboot(t):
    s=t['start']
    return bool(s.get('reboot_results')) or any(
        c['operation']=='delivery_reboot' for c in s['calls']) or any(
        x['event']['kind']=='collect_reboot' or (
            x['event']['kind']=='request' and x['event']['operation']=='delivery_reboot')
        for x in t['steps'])

def dispatch(t):
    if rescue(t): return 'dedicated'
    if reboot(t): return 'reboot'
    return 'stage1'
```

title: collect_jobs reports a call whose record read did not complete as failed
description:
## What
`collect_jobs` (`src/harness/run.rs`) reports a call whose job-record read, parse, validation or
evidence append did not complete as `{"call":1,"job":"…","failed":true,"why":"…"}`. The entry names
the call and says `failed`, while the call stays unresolved. `CNF-29` says an interrupted call is
not reported as failed, and `spec/CONTEXT.md`'s "Unresolved" entry lists "failed" under _Avoid_.

twr-ggw.69's held answer reports the same situations as `not_read` (nothing was read) or
`not_journaled` (the record was read and its evidence was not appended). Collection keeps the
shape twr-ggw.12 gave it, so the two reports of one read differ.

## Needs deciding
Whether collection's per-call entry takes the held answer's `not_read` / `not_journaled` shape, and
the README's description of collection with it.

## Spec
CNF-29, STA-8, STA-20

title: The seed-backup failed-append text says the completion was not recorded when a landed move replays it
description:
## What
When a seed-backup completion's append fails, `Local::seed_backup_complete` (`src/store.rs`)
tells the operator "The completion was not recorded.", and at create also "The seed-backup
ceremony is still owed." That holds when the move did nothing. It is false when the move landed
and then reported failure, as `MemoryStorage`'s `Fault::LandThenFail` models and Chromium's
`move()` allows: the store's README says such a record "is replayed after the restart". After the
reload and unlock the page asks for, the completion is in the journal, the ceremony is no longer
owed, and allocation is admitted.

The worker's own state is right: nothing is applied in memory, so `STA-23`'s "A failed append
leaves no completion." holds for this worker, and allocation stays refused until the restart.
Only the page's claim about durability goes beyond what the harness knows when it makes it.

## Needs deciding
Whether the failed-append text says the completion may or may not have been recorded, and that
reload and unlock show which, with a host test under `Fault::LandThenFail` for both completions
at create and on re-display.

## Spec
STA-23, STA-3, SEC-2

title: No ticket owns the real recurring cost the setup's batch card shows
description:
## What
The setup's batch card (twr-ggw.10) shows each machine entry's recurring cost and the setup's
monthly and annual totals. The approval record journals that cost as the approved cost beside
which twr-ggw.21, twr-ggw.32 and twr-ggw.41 later show an invoice amount (`ARC-30`). Today the
entries and their costs are compiled fixture data (`dispatch::fixture_setup` in
`src/dispatch/setup.rs`: 1000 and 2000 sat per month), labelled in the README as an
implementation reading. `ARC-15` asks the batch screen to show the setup's true recurring cost.

No open ticket reads a vendor's real price for an entry before the operator approves:
- twr-ggw.14 supplies sessions and goals;
- twr-ggw.21, twr-ggw.32 and twr-ggw.41 read invoices after approval;
- twr-ggw.22 grows a set on a card that shows the cost, without saying where it comes from.

## Needs deciding
- Which ticket reads each entry's real recurring cost (vendor, product, region), from what
  source, before the card renders.
- How a price that changes between approval and create is handled.
- When non-fixture amounts reach the page, they must be shown exactly as journaled.
  - `MachineEntry`'s `cost.amount` is a `u64`, and the worker parses the module's report with
    `JSON.parse` (`reportStore` in `www/worker.js`).
  - So the page (`renderSetup` in `www/boot.js`) shows an amount above 9007199254740991
    rounded.
  - Every real sat amount is below that bound, since bitcoin's whole supply is, and production
    journals only the fixture prices today, so no operator path reaches it yet.
  - The owner of real prices bounds the amount or carries it exactly.

## Spec
ARC-15, ARC-30, ADR-0009

title: Binding admits an allocation identity that is a tombstone
description:
## What
twr-ggw.11's binding act (`Store::bind` in `src/store.rs`) admits an approved entry when its
exact allocation identity is listed under the current seed, whatever that entry's status.
Exposure replay (`Store::replay_exposure`) applies the same rule. So an identity whose
allocation entry is `failed` or `destroyed`, `STA-22b`'s tombstones, can still be bound:
- the session is given that identity's client key (`SEC-5` row 3);
- the exposure ledger gains an entry for it.

The binding ticket deliberately took presence as the rule and left status handling at binding to
the ticket that journals creates. twr-ggw.21, the ticket that work named, does not carry it.

No operator path reaches this today. Allocation's `Failed` and `Destroyed` observations have no
production writer yet, so only a replayed `Restore` that lists a tombstoned machine identity can
bring one into the store. It becomes reachable once creates (twr-ggw.21), destroys and abandonment
(twr-ggw.31) or sheet import (twr-ggw.27) journal tombstones.

`STA-22b` says "The journal owns a seed identifier, derivation version, next unused index for
each role family (machines, passes, handoffs), and allocated entries, including tombstones for
failed or destroyed allocations."

`SEC-1` says "A machine is bound to a session by provisioning it; by re-entry, on a maintained
machine only; or by the recovery ladder's escalation, which re-binds a half-provisioning machine
to the successor session under `ARC-16`'s condition."

## Needs deciding
- Whether binding refuses an identity whose entry is `failed` or `destroyed`, and which ticket
  owns that refusal.
- Whether replay refuses an exposure record naming an identity that was a tombstone at that
  point of the journal.
- A `reserved` identity must stay bindable, because provisioning binds before the create is
  sent (`SEC-1`). What happens to a live session whose machine's create then fails is part of
  the same decision.

## Spec
SEC-1, STA-22b, CNF-7

title: CNF-67's unpinned unsigned-package refusal is observable only on the live Arch machine, and no ticket records it
description:
## What
twr-ggw.13 refuses, before anything is sent and with its own journal record, a box-plane command
that lowers pacman's signature checking in the two literal forms `ARC-25a` names, on a machine
where an installation with no artifact pin stands. It does not show an unsigned package refused.
That refusal is the distribution's own: no fixture box plane runs pacman, and the CI runners
(`ubuntu-latest`) carry neither pacman nor Nix. What twr-ggw.13 gives is the lowering refusal plus
Arch's stock `pacman.conf` vendored byte for byte from Arch's packaging commit `c8ccc368`
(`tests/vectors/pacman-c8ccc368.conf`), which sets `SigLevel = Required DatabaseOptional` and
`LocalFileSigLevel = Optional`.

Its implementation reading: "an unsigned package" is an unsigned **repository** package, refused
by the distribution's stock checking. Stock Arch accepts a local unsigned `pacman -U` file
(`LocalFileSigLevel = Optional`); the harness neither refuses that nor raises the setting.

Two tickets expect more than that:
- twr-ggw.49's admission record lists "CNF-67, unpinned: an unsigned package and a lowering command
  are refused (twr-ggw.13)" among the fixture cases that pass in CI.
- twr-ggw.51's live run installs plain Arch unpinned, but none of its criteria names `CNF-67`.

`CNF-67` says "On an unpinned installation (`ARC-25`), the distribution's own signature checking
stays on: an unsigned package is refused, and a command lowering the check is refused before it is
sent." The admission paragraph of `07-conformance.md` says "Live-only checks are completed during
that run, not asserted before it."

## Needs deciding
- Whether twr-ggw.51 observes, on the live Arch machine with the distribution's checking left on,
  an unsigned repository package refused, and records it as `CNF-67`'s unpinned evidence.
- Whether twr-ggw.49's line is amended to the lowering refusal as twr-ggw.13's fixture case, with
  the observed refusal named as live-only and owed by twr-ggw.51.
- Whether a local unsigned `pacman -U` file on stock Arch is among the unsigned packages `CNF-67`
  requires refused. If it is, that is a question for the specification: the harness would have to
  refuse such a command or raise `LocalFileSigLevel`, and `ARC-25a` asks for neither.

## Spec
CNF-67, ARC-25, ARC-25a, ARC-24

title: Typed operations on a fixture adapter, behind the unresolved barrier
description:
## What to build
A fixture adapter's reads, create and running-system changes are approved on structured facts, recorded before they are sent, and confirmed only by observable state. While one is unresolved, the barrier on its approved machine entry refuses the same effect however it is requested again, and a running-system change stops box-plane dispatch to that machine. The dispatch core runs the companion comparison over the stage1 dispatch traces; twr-i6k.3 owns rescue-rule traces and twr-i6k.11 owns the remaining delivery_reboot traces.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Killing the worker between record and send leaves the record [CNF-28 (fixture adapter), SEC-12].
- [ ] A lost response to a fixture create leaves it unresolved; a second request for it under a new call id, through another tool, after replay or from a later session is refused, and so is a second allocation index for the same entry; a different approved entry stays permitted [CNF-29, STA-24].
- [ ] A read naming the resource stays permitted, and a status read whose journal append fails leaves the barrier standing [CNF-29, STA-24].
- [ ] A fixture reset or reinstall stops box-plane dispatch from its intent until confirmation. A disposition lifts that stop only as its continuation permits [STA-24].
- [ ] Each operation is approved on its facts, never on command text [ARC-4].
- [ ] With a fixture call that changes what the machine is running left unresolved and disposed, a box-plane command to that machine is refused under a destructive reinstall and under abandonment: STA-24's destructive stop covers every box-plane job, whoever starts it [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] Within the disposed calls' reach, every cloud-plane operation the continuation does not permit is refused: "A destructive reinstall permits only the reinstall, abandonment only the abandonment flow"; an operation outside that reach is neither restricted by it nor ends it [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] With a fixture call that changes what the machine is running left unresolved and disposed under either continuation that continues, a box-plane command is dispatched, and the same operation requested again under a fresh call id is dispatched where no other call is unresolved: "Continuing as if done and continuing as if not done restrict nothing" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] For either continuation that continues, the harness reports the operator's recorded assumption for the operator's screen, "never written as success, failure, zero spend or non-execution"; rendering on screen is twr-ggw.66's [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] With an unresolved fixture create disposed to continue under either continuation that continues, a box-plane command is dispatched: "a disposed create, activation or key registration bars nothing on the box plane"; this ticket exercises the create case [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] With any stage-1 call disposed toward a destructive reinstall or abandonment, an unresolved box-plane command included, the model's box-plane command to that machine is refused, "whatever the disposed call was" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] Across CNF-110's stage-1 disposition cases, a status read is dispatched and does not end the restriction: "A read and the inference request are never restricted"; a model's command refused before the read is still refused after it [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] Across CNF-110's stage-1 disposition cases, a pinned SSH attempt is dispatched and does not end the restriction: "Reads stay permitted throughout"; a model's command refused before the attempt is still refused after it [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] Across CNF-110's stage-1 disposition cases, the collection of job records is dispatched and does not end the restriction: reads stay permitted, "the pinned SSH attempt that is `STG-4`'s third predicate and the collection of job records among them"; a model's command refused before the collection is still refused after it (folded from twr-ggw.68) [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] For stage-1 continuations, the restriction ends at the dispatch of the reinstall or of the destroy (the stop that stands in for one), its intent durably appended, and not before: "from then on that call's own barrier governs"; from that intent the call's own barrier refuses and nothing is refused under the disposition [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] A disposition naming no call, a call already settled or a call on another resource is refused and journals nothing; the harness reports for the operator's screen "the refusal, the record that settled the call if one did, and what is unresolved now"; rendering on screen is twr-ggw.66's [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] A disposition naming some of several unresolved calls leaves the others barring: "the unnamed ones stay unresolved and keep their barrier" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] A replacement naming the calls the standing disposition disposed is accepted, and the harness reports what it replaces for the operator's screen: "One disposition stands per resource, the latest, and its continuation is the one in force"; with a destructive reinstall replaced by abandonment, the reinstall is refused; rendering on screen is twr-ggw.66's [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] A replayed journal already holding a disposition that the naming test refuses, the replacement exception included, "ends no call and restricts nothing"; calls it named that remain unresolved keep their barrier, and the harness reports the refused record for the operator's screen; rendering on screen is twr-ggw.66's [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] A valid replacement is still the one in force after a worker restart and journal replay: "the continuation in force after a restart is the latest valid one" [CNF-110, STA-24, STA-7].
- [ ] Evidence appended after a disposition about a call it disposed is journaled and reported and "neither reopens the call nor removes the disposition"; the disposition stands until its continuation is dispatched or the operator replaces it [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] The production dispatch core passes its `stage1` bucket of `dispatch-witnesses-v6.json`, schema 6, at d029ebd: 31 witnesses and 286 enumerated traces; dedicated: 54 witnesses / 184 enumerated traces left to twr-i6k.3; reboot: 12 witnesses / 0 enumerated traces left to twr-i6k.11. The three buckets sum to 97 witnesses and 470 enumerated traces. Bound: 3 events over an alphabet of 8, filtered to distinct request call ids. Use the single step test below in all three comparisons: rescue first, then reboot content in start or steps, then stage1. Presence of empty reboot_results or nonempty current_installations alone never routes a trace. Every refused/admitted pair stays whole. Unknown schema, kind, operation, continuation, source, outcome or projection member fails naming the trace. Compare every outcome and projection at every step, starting with the start records. Measured vocabulary: continuations: abandonment, as_if_done, as_if_not_done, destructive_reinstall; kinds: dispose, read, replay, request; operations: create, destroy, exec, inference, read, reinstall, reset; outcome_members: dispatch, disposition, refusal, settled; projection_members: associations, calls, current_installations, dispatched, dispositions, durable, prerequisite_records, reboot_results, reinstall_approvals, reinstall_withdrawals, reset_offer, standing, unresolved; refusal_reasons: barrier, continuation; request_operations: create, destroy, exec, inference, read, reinstall, reset; sources: adapter_read, job_record; start_members: associations, calls, current_installations, dispatched, dispositions, durable, prerequisite_records, reboot_results, reinstall_approvals, reinstall_withdrawals, reset_offer, standing, unresolved. Each pair below is a negative control: production matches the refused side and differs from the admitted side; commandHold: TauWeb.Dispatch.second_command_held versus TauWeb.Dispatch.second_command_without_hold; sessionDestroyRefused: TauWeb.Dispatch.session_destroy_under_abandonment_refused versus TauWeb.Dispatch.session_destroy_lifts_abandonment_without_guard; resourceKey: TauWeb.Dispatch.same_action_new_call_id_refused versus TauWeb.Dispatch.same_action_new_call_id_admitted; resourceKey: TauWeb.Dispatch.second_index_same_entry_refused versus TauWeb.Dispatch.second_index_same_entry_admitted; endedBelowSucceeded: TauWeb.Dispatch.boot_id_change_not_success_refused versus TauWeb.Dispatch.boot_id_change_not_success_admitted; durableBeforeApply: TauWeb.Dispatch.resolution_append_failed_refused versus TauWeb.Dispatch.resolution_append_failed_admitted; dispositionBindsContinuation: TauWeb.Dispatch.disposition_one_continuation_refused versus TauWeb.Dispatch.disposition_unrestricted_admitted; lapse: TauWeb.Dispatch.read_does_not_lift_abandonment versus TauWeb.Dispatch.read_lifts_abandonment_without_guard; destructiveStops: TauWeb.Dispatch.destructive_choice_stops_commands versus TauWeb.Dispatch.command_preempts_reinstall_without_guard; reach: TauWeb.Dispatch.read_and_inference_never_restricted versus TauWeb.Dispatch.read_and_inference_restricted_without_guard; dispositionOwnResource: TauWeb.Dispatch.disposition_names_own_unresolved_calls versus TauWeb.Dispatch.disposition_ends_call_elsewhere_without_guard; reach: TauWeb.Dispatch.replacement_in_force versus TauWeb.Dispatch.replaced_continuation_dispatched_without_guard. The record names the rule, file, bound, spec and implementation revisions. Make CNF-3's three breaks once by hand and record each red trace: flip an expected outcome in a scratch file, remove or empty the file, and introduce an unrecognised event kind or outcome. This split is an implementation reading of ADR-0032. The file's bound is covered only by the three runs together: witnesses by all three, enumerated traces by twr-ggw.8 and twr-i6k.3. The reboot bucket has zero enumerated traces because the alphabet has neither delivery_reboot nor collect_reboot; its 12 witnesses are its whole comparison. Dispatch witnesses omit ARC-43's pending-delivery-check hold and lifecycle reads; an exec after settled delivery_reboot represents one after the verdict. Those integrated cases need separate evidence [CNF-3, ADR-0032, STA-20, STA-24, ARC-43].

```python
def rescue(t):
    start=t['start']; dispositions=list(start['dispositions'])
    if start['reset_offer'] or any(start[k] for k in
            ('reinstall_approvals','reinstall_withdrawals','prerequisite_records')):
        return True
    for step in t['steps']:
        e=step['event']; kind=e['kind']
        if kind in ('reset_prereqs','approve_reinstall','withdraw_reinstall'):
            return True
        if kind in ('request','read'):
            if e['operation'] in ('activate','register_key'): return True
            if kind=='request' and e['operation']=='reset' and any(
                    d['continuation']=='destructive_reinstall' for d in dispositions):
                return True
        if kind=='dispose': dispositions.append(e)
    return False

def reboot(t):
    s=t['start']
    return bool(s.get('reboot_results')) or any(
        c['operation']=='delivery_reboot' for c in s['calls']) or any(
        x['event']['kind']=='collect_reboot' or (
            x['event']['kind']=='request' and x['event']['operation']=='delivery_reboot')
        for x in t['steps'])

def dispatch(t):
    if rescue(t): return 'dedicated'
    if reboot(t): return 'reboot'
    return 'stage1'
```

- [ ] A replacement may omit calls: they stay settled under the replaced record, outcome unknown, add no restriction and can never be named again. Return the dropped calls for twr-ggw.66's screen; test replay and the LNVPS fixture as well [STA-24, CNF-110].

- [ ] A session destroy under standing abandonment is refused; the deterministic flow still waits on every undisposed call and dispatches only after the barrier permits it [STA-24, SEC-4, CNF-110].

- [ ] The stage1 bucket exercises commandHold: four refused box-plane requests in named witnesses and 28 in the enumeration. Wait on twr-ggw.69 for its dispatch check [STA-20, CNF-40, ADR-0032].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.69 — the commandHold guard required by the stage1 comparison
- twr-ggw.58 — prerequisite behaviour used by these criteria
- twr-ggw.72 — requirements at spec 8869ade
- twr-ggw.6 — Allocation: an index is journaled before use and never reused
- twr-ggw.7 — Box-plane commands go through the journal and survive a killed worker

## Spec
SEC-12, ARC-4, STA-4, STA-5, STA-8, STA-24, ADR-0032, CNF-3, CNF-28, CNF-29, CNF-110, SEC-4, STA-7, ARC-43, CNF-40, STA-20

title: Commands that lower pacman's signature checking outside the two literal forms are sent
description:
## What
twr-ggw.13 refuses a box-plane command that lowers pacman's signature checking only in two literal
forms, on a machine where an installation with no artifact pin stands: a `SigLevel`,
`LocalFileSigLevel` or `RemoteFileSigLevel` directive followed, later on the same raw line, by an
`=` and then by a whole `Never`, `PackageNever` or `DatabaseNever` (a signature level of never) or
`TrustAll`, `PackageTrustAll` or `DatabaseTrustAll` (pacman's equivalent of an
untrusted-repository flag; pacman has no such command-line flag). It reads raw command bytes line
by line and evaluates no shell (`src/modes.rs`, `lowering`).

Its README states what it does not catch, and each of these can lower the distribution's checking
and is sent:
- a directive or lowering word split by quoting, a brace or an escape (`Sig"Level"`, `Nev'er'`,
  `Nev{er,}`, `printf 'Required\tNever'`);
- line continuations;
- a lowering word that never appears literally after the directive's `=` on that raw line
  (`SigLevel = $LEVEL`, `SigLevel = $(printf 'Nev%s' er)`, `L=Never; echo "SigLevel = $L"`);
- a raw line whose first non-whitespace byte is `#` but which the shell does not read as a comment
  (the `#` closing a string quoted across the line before);
- encodings (base64, printf escapes);
- a configuration written elsewhere and pulled in by `Include =` or `--config`;
- substitutions that never spell the directive (`sed 's/Required/Never/'`);
- a bare `SigLevel = Optional`, which admits an unsigned package;
- a commented `#SigLevel = Never` uncommented by a later stage;
- scripts fetched at run time.

`ARC-25a` says "Its distribution's own package-signature checking still stays on: the unpinned
mode waives the bundle's pin, never signature enforcement, and the harness never sends a command
that lowers it (an untrusted-repository flag, a signature level of never)." `CNF-67` says "On an
unpinned installation (`ARC-25`), the distribution's own signature checking stays on: an unsigned
package is refused, and a command lowering the check is refused before it is sent."

## Needs deciding
- Whether "a command that lowers it" reaches beyond the two forms the parenthesis names, and if
  so which: a bare `Optional` presence level; a substitution that never spells the directive;
  `Include =` and `--config`.
- Whether a byte matcher is the right place for the wider set, or whether the check belongs on the
  machine, for example reading pacman's effective configuration before each package operation.
  ADR-0002 rejected static classification of the shell the model emits as a load-bearing control:
  "Rejected because classifying arbitrary shell by danger is undecidable and adversarially
  fragile — variable expansion, `eval`, base64, a `curl` piped to a shell each defeat it." If the
  specification leaves this open, it goes back to the specification repository.

## Spec
ARC-25a, CNF-67, ADR-0002

title: No ticket re-accepts an installation with no artifact pin at a reinstall
description:
## What
twr-ggw.13 accepts the mode **An installation with no artifact pin** only inside a machine's first binding,
in one record with it. At the fixture adapter's reinstall it restates every standing mode and does
not accept the installation mode again; the mode keeps standing as the machine's history. No
ticket builds the re-acceptance:
- twr-ggw.45 (the LNVPS reinstall) restates the standing modes at the reinstall and accepts none,
  although stage 1 reinstalls plain Arch unpinned, which is a new installation.
- `CNF-93`'s jump-host reinstall case is stage 2's.

`SEC-14` says "A mode is accepted by the session that does what it governs, before doing it." and
"An installation with no artifact pin and a first contact from a jump host are the machine's
history: every later set that includes the machine is shown them at binding and restates them,
and accepts them again only for a reinstall, which is a new installation and a new first contact
(`CHN-R6`)." Among `CNF-93`'s cases is a reinstall on the jump-host route, accepted again as an
installation and a first contact before it is sent. `STA-16` says:

> Installation pin status and pin routes are the history modes of `SEC-14`, and a Restore does
> not reapprove them — only a reinstall, a new installation, is accepted afresh; the restored
> conduct modes were the exporting session's, which ended, and a re-entering session accepts its
> own rather than reapproving them, while what they left live stays "unknown since export".

## Needs deciding
- Whether a reinstall of a machine whose installation has no artifact pin needs that mode accepted
  again, by the session that sends the reinstall and before it is sent; and whether the earlier
  installation's acceptance stops standing then, or both stand.
- Which ticket owns it: twr-ggw.45 at LNVPS, and the jump-host route at stage 2.

## Spec
SEC-14, STA-16, CNF-93, CHN-R6, ARC-25

title: Accepting an installation with no artifact pin is not tied to a distribution the bundle carries no pin for
description:
## What
twr-ggw.13 accepts the mode **An installation with no artifact pin** inside a machine's first
binding (`Store::bind_with_modes`). Nothing in this build chooses or installs a distribution, so
the acceptance names none and is not checked against the bundle's pins. The bundle pins Alpine
(`spec/bundle/artifact-alpine.toml`).

`ARC-25` says "Installing a distribution the bundle carries no pin for is an acceptable weaker mode
(`SEC-14`): the operator chooses it up front, from what the bundle lacks, and the machine is
recorded and shown as **unpinned** from then on." `SEC-14` says "The operator chooses a mode from
what the bundle or the vendor lacks — no pin for this distribution, no adapter for this vendor, no
out-of-band route at this vendor, no brief for this software — or from what the set needs, more
than one machine — before the first contact it governs: with any machine of the set for a mode
accepted as the set is bound, with the added machine for one accepted as the set grows (`SEC-1`)."
ADR-0035 says "Artifact pinning stays BLOCKING wherever a pin exists; what the operator may choose,
up front, is a distribution that has none."

## Needs deciding
- Where a machine's distribution is fixed relative to its first binding, so that the acceptance
  names it, and that accepting the mode for a distribution the bundle pins (Alpine today) is
  refused.
- Which ticket owns it: the first to choose a distribution for a machine (the Alpine install,
  twr-i6k.5; the goal-driven fixture install, twr-ggw.16; the live Arch install, twr-ggw.51).

## Spec
ARC-25, ARC-24, SEC-14, ADR-0035

title: Choose who sets the session inference key spend cap and expiry
description: ARC-31a and CNF-69 require a spend cap and an expiry for each procured session inference key. The pinned specification supplies neither values nor an owner for choosing them. Procured inference uses named implementation constants (0.10 account units and 900 seconds). Decide the values and who sets them before claiming the live account check in twr-ggw.51.

title: The operator enters the inference account credential: held encrypted at rest, given to no session
description:
## What to build
The served build gives the operator a control to enter the inference account credential of a balance already funded at the aggregator `bundle/inference.toml` names. The harness worker commits it encrypted at rest before holding it, through the production store method twr-ggw.17 added, and session key minting (twr-ggw.17) then uses it. Today only a tracer-only entry reaches that method, with no operator control or page message.

Funding the balance stays outside the harness at this stage: `STG-18` says "**Inference funding.** Assumed already funded." `SEC-5` row 14's origin is "Operator, on funding an account-free balance". `ARC-30`'s assisted invoice for inference credits is not built here. Exporting the credential in the recovery sheet stays twr-ggw.27's.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] While the store is unlocked and outside the seed-backup ceremony, the page offers the entry; the worker commits one encrypted record before it holds the credential, and the page clears its copy of the value on every exit. `ARC-31a` says "It is the operator's, held encrypted at rest and exported in the recovery sheet (`STA-16`), because it is spendable balance and nothing re-derives it." [SEC-5 row 14, ARC-31a]
- [ ] Entry while locked or during the seed-backup ceremony is refused before anything is stored, saying why. Entry sends nothing to the aggregator; the first account read stays twr-ggw.17's, before the first mint.
- [ ] No session holding, model request body or plaintext journal record carries the credential, shown by the held-credential scan. `ARC-31a` says "**A session MUST NOT receive the account credential, and no model sees either tier.**"
- [ ] The page never shows the value back. It states that the credential is bearer and cannot be revoked, and that only the recovery sheet keeps it across a lost store. `SEC-5` row 14's "How it dies" cell reads "Spent down or abandoned — **it is bearer and cannot be revoked**".
- [ ] Implementation reading: a held credential can be replaced only while no session is live; the replacement is journaled before it takes effect and supersedes the earlier record, and a replacement while a session is live is refused, saying why.
- [ ] The served build contains the operator path; `check-absence` still finds no tracer-only export in it [STG-10, STG-14].

## Blocked by
Nothing open.

## Spec
ARC-31a, SEC-5 row 14, STG-18, STA-16, CNF-69, CNF-70, STG-10, STG-14

title: The cold-probe session-end browser case can fail by timing, and its refusal check cannot catch the unfenced probe
description:
The browser case "session end fences a cold probe queued ahead of the end writer"
(`tracer/src/session_end_cases.rs`, `cold_probe`) can fail for the wrong reason, and only one of
its checks catches the defect it guards.

- "revoke itself is sent" reads the aggregator's requests once, right after a 50 ms poll saw the
  revoke's dedicated probe. The revoke's POST follows that probe only after its OPTIONS answer,
  the route record and the revoke intent's append, so on the fixed code the check can run before
  the POST arrives. On `8dbfcee`'s code the same check also failed in the recorded red run
  (README I40), which shows it is timing-sensitive.
- "stopped inference refuses its cold probe" passes with the probe fence removed (I40's red log
  shows it `[ok]`): without the fence the account read is refused "sessions ended" instead, with
  no call id. So the case's red rests on the OPTIONS count alone, and that count cannot tell the
  inference's probe from the revoke's (both carry the same placeholder).

Make the case wait for the revoke's POST before judging it, and tell the two probes apart (for
example by their order relative to the revoke's POST), so the case goes red on the unfixed probe
for the probe itself and does not go red on the fixed code by timing.

title: A goal is not refused under a profile that declares an independence bound (CNF-102)
description:
## What is missing
CNF-102 is a stage-1 BLOCKING item, and one of its clauses has no owning ticket and no code.
`CNF-102` says "A goal steers one session's bound set (`ARC-11a`, `STG-21`): it is journaled with
that session and its source, the interface offers no import, sharing or reuse of one, and a goal
is refused for a machine under a profile that declares an independence bound." `ARC-11a` says
"A goal MUST be refused for a machine under a profile that declares an independence bound."

twr-ggw.14 built the goal record, its source and the absence of import, sharing and reuse. The
independence-bound refusal was not among its acceptance criteria, so it was not built: goal entry
(`Store::enter_goal`, `src/store/goals.rs`) checks no profile's independence-bound slot. Today
every setup entry runs under the ad-hoc profile, which declares none, so no reachable goal is
wrongly admitted. A machine under a profile whose independence-bound slot holds a relation
(btc-policy's) would still be admitted a goal.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A goal entered for a session whose bound set holds a machine under a profile that declares
an independence bound is refused, writing nothing; replay refuses such a record [CNF-102,
ARC-11a].
- [ ] A test fails when the refusal is removed.

title: No ticket owns the operator's approval of a typed operation the model requests
description:
## What is missing
No ticket owns the operator's approval of a typed operation the model requests. `ARC-43` lists
"`request_typed_operation` (a cloud-plane operation, approved on facts)" among the model's tools.
`ARC-4` says "Approving an *operation* means seeing structured facts about one action and
permitting it — available only where an adapter types the action, or where the harness composed
the job itself and shows its facts on a card (`ARC-43`'s `place_secret`)."

twr-ggw.14 routes the model's `request_typed_operation` through the binding and barrier checks
before any approval, then refuses every such request as awaiting the operator's approval. It
records nothing. No operator act, card or queue exists to approve the request's exact facts, so
a model-requested typed operation can never be dispatched. twr-ggw.21 (create and payment),
twr-ggw.66 (the disposition screen) and twr-i6k.10 (reinstall approval withdrawal) each cover
other approvals, not this one.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Decide and record which ticket owns the operator's approval of a model-requested typed
operation on its exact facts, its screen, and how its tool result completes [ARC-4, ARC-43,
STA-24].

title: The goal outcome label's unresolved precedence has no check
description:
## What is missing
The goal card's loop-outcome label has an untested precedence rule. `www/boot.js` labels an
outcome with `unresolved: true` as unresolved before it considers a refusal. The README's
"outcome labels" implementation reading claims that order. No host or browser check covers the
unresolved branch, or the neutral `Goal loop ended.` fallback. Swapping the unresolved and
refused branches stays green.

An unresolved inference request can carry both `unresolved: true` and a refusal, for example an
account read whose answer was lost. With the branches swapped, the page would describe an
unresolved call as refused. `CNF-29` says "An interrupted call is recorded as **unresolved**, is
not retried automatically, and is not reported as failed."

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A check drives a goal turn whose outcome is unresolved and carries a refusal, and asserts
the label says unresolved and not refused [CNF-29, STA-8].
- [ ] The check fails when the unresolved and refused branches are swapped.

title: One credential-redaction boundary before the journal and the model
description:
## What to build
Every typed-adapter response, and every injected response standing in for an untyped one, passes one credential-redaction boundary before it is written to the journal or reaches model context. The boundary redacts a root password a typed adapter's response carries and scans for exact copies of every credential the harness holds. It is tested with an injected root password and with CNF-17's injected response fixture, which does not enable untyped calls.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A root password injected into a fixture adapter's response is absent from the journal and from model context [CNF-14, SEC-5 row 9].
- [ ] An injected response carrying a harness-held credential is redacted, by exact-value scan, before it reaches the model or the record [CNF-17, SEC-5].
- [ ] Every adapter routes its responses through the one boundary; a test fails if a response reaches the journal or the model by another path.
- [ ] No harness-held credential appears in a request to the app origin, in a model request body or in any log [STG-10].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.8 — Typed operations on a fixture adapter, behind the unresolved barrier

## Spec
SEC-5 row 9, SEC-5, STG-10, CNF-14, CNF-17

comments.author: user
comments.text:
Landed in 3dd4d6d: one credential-redaction boundary (src/redaction.rs) behind Store::operation_response, which every typed adapter response and the injected stand-in pass before the journal append and before the output is handed on.

Implementation readings, each labelled in README "The credential-redaction boundary":
- Exact copy (CNF-17): raw bytes only, exactly as held. Hex, HEX, base64, base64url, JSON-escaped, partial and transformed copies pass. A random 32- or 64-byte key essentially cannot appear verbatim in UTF-8 JSON, so in typed JSON bodies the scan catches credentials held as text; the injected arbitrary-byte stand-in exercises the binary keys.
- Marker: one fixed visible marker, `<redacted>`, for both mechanisms. A declared root-password field keeps its name; absent stays absent, null stays null. No claim that the rest of the response is scrubbed.
- Journal: a new `operation_response` record (call, lowercase-hex redacted body), appended after the typed intent and before return. It settles nothing, at most one per call; replay refuses a record naming no earlier typed call, a box-plane call, a repeat, a non-lowercase-hex body or an extra member. Older journals contain none and replay unchanged.
- Model context: the boundary's returned output is its stand-in. No model, tool or model request exists (twr-ggw.14, twr-ggw.17), so STG-10's model-request-body clause has no body to check in this build.
- Two mechanisms: root-password redaction covers only the fields the typed adapter declares (RFC 6901 pointers; the fixture declares /root_password), and a body that is not JSON is refused with no record. The injected stand-in gets the scan alone, with no password heuristic.
- Held set: enumerated by the store at call time: the seed's bytes and mnemonic, the data key, every credential given to a live session, and roles 0-4 at every identity listed under the current seed, any status. The passphrase and wrapping key are cleared before any response can pass, and their lifetimes are not extended to scan for them. Later tickets add the vendor credential, the session inference key (twr-ggw.17) and the role-5 key (twr-ggw.47) to that enumeration.
- Re-serialization: with declared fields the body is re-serialized by serde_json's defaults (sorted members, rewritten number text, integers past 64 bits read as floats). A recorded typed response keeps values, not the vendor's bytes.
- CNF-17's stage-1 evidence is the host-only injected response, journaled against a fixture typed call; no untyped call or scope is built. The repeat against real untyped responses is still owed before scopes are enabled.

Evidence: host tests check absence with needles derived independently via bip39/bip32 in raw, hex, HEX, base64 and base64url, including embedded alignments. They search every decrypted record, the decoded response bodies and the returned output. Mutations shown red, then green: boundary bypass (root password found in decrypted record 9), field redaction off, scan off (all 16 held values found), the data key dropped from the set, the Redacted field made pub (compile_fail doctest fails), a console leak of the passphrase in boot.js (tracer no-plaintext case fails), and a planted root password in dist/served (check-absence fails). All gates passed, including the full web job ending in TRACER PASS; check-install-disks.py --baseline failed as required.

title: The pinned tunnel: TLS to a vendor API inside the browser, over the relay
description:
## What to build
TLS is terminated in the harness worker against an issuer pin shipped in the bundle, and rides the relay as ciphertext. A valid certificate from another issuer halts, the relay fixture observes only ciphertext, and an issuer pin that no longer matches gives an actionable failure naming rotation. If twr-y8a's the browser-CORS observation finds LNVPS refusing a browser origin, this ticket moves into stage 1, twr-ggw.32 waits on it, and CNF-62 joins twr-ggw.49's admission record.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A valid certificate from a different issuer halts the call before any byte is sent [CNF-62, CHN-12a].
- [ ] The relay fixture observes only ciphertext for a tunnelled call [CNF-63].
- [ ] An issuer pin that no longer matches produces a failure naming rotation as the likely cause, never an opaque network error [CNF-64].
- [ ] The issuer pin is a store of exactly one authority, taken from the bundle [CHN-12a].

title: The operator withdraws a dedicated reinstall approval
description:
## What to build

title: The delivery reboot: boot-change settlement and the pending delivery check
description:
## What to build
Implement ARC-43's harness-only delivery_reboot outside LNVPS, with the operator's yes journaled in its intent, boot-change collection as its result, and ARC-43's pending-delivery-check hold until the verdict or the operator's journaled stop. Run the reboot bucket of the production dispatch comparison. The dedicated applicability row owns these cases; no stage-1 ticket waits on this ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Offer only for enabled-survives-reboot with no co-declared running-at-delivery service, after the last placement and with a fresh explicit yes. Reject model requests and supplied command text. A command in flight at the yes invokes STA-20's unresolved-command hold: append no intent, start no pending-delivery-check hold and ask for yes again at the eventual first issue [ARC-43, STA-20, CNF-53].
- [ ] Collect that call's own job record for that machine on a boot different from its recorded boot. Settle durably by observed boot change, never exit status or cause, even with an incomplete record that carries its own boot, and regardless of exit code. Old-boot exit or Ended, missing record, no recorded boot, wrong machine, wrong call or missing yes settles nothing. Failed settlement append keeps it unresolved through replay; durable append settles on replay [ARC-43, STA-20, STA-3, CNF-53, CNF-55].
- [ ] Reconnect on the pin and collect, visibly and stoppably. ARC-43's pending-delivery-check hold starts with yes plus intent and lasts through the durable delivery verdict, including after reboot settlement. Its held result names the pending check. A delivery-check command ending without exit stays unresolved; its continuing disposition releases only STA-20's unresolved-command hold. Without a verdict, commands stay held by ARC-43's pending-delivery-check hold until an operator-journaled stop, shown as stopped and never pass [ARC-43, STA-20, STA-24, CNF-53].
- [ ] Refuse the harness-composed delivery_reboot under both destructive reinstall and abandonment dispositions, whoever starts it and whatever call was disposed. Permitted status/SSH/record reads still pass. A late new-boot record after a destructive disposition neither removes it nor resumes commands [ARC-43, STA-24, CNF-53, CNF-110, ADR-0050].
- [ ] CNF-40's held-harness-job case: under STA-20's unresolved-command hold, no intent or queue; the visible flow composes a first issue afresh after release, with fresh yes, once under one intent. A stopped wait leaves nothing armed across replay; only the operator resumes the stopped flow [STA-20, ARC-43, CNF-40].
- [ ] The production dispatch core passes its `reboot` bucket of `dispatch-witnesses-v6.json`, schema 6, at d029ebd: 12 witnesses and 0 enumerated traces; stage1: 31 witnesses / 286 enumerated traces left to twr-ggw.8; dedicated: 54 witnesses / 184 enumerated traces left to twr-i6k.3. The three buckets sum to 97 witnesses and 470 enumerated traces. Bound: 3 events over an alphabet of 8, filtered to distinct request call ids. Use the single step test below in all three comparisons: rescue first, then reboot content in start or steps, then stage1. Presence of empty reboot_results or nonempty current_installations alone never routes a trace. Every refused/admitted pair stays whole. Unknown schema, kind, operation, continuation, source, outcome or projection member fails naming the trace. Compare every outcome and projection at every step, starting with the start records. Measured vocabulary: continuations: abandonment, destructive_reinstall; kinds: collect_reboot, dispose, read, replay, request; operations: delivery_reboot, exec; outcome_members: dispatch, disposition, refusal, settled; projection_members: associations, calls, current_installations, dispatched, dispositions, durable, prerequisite_records, reboot_results, reinstall_approvals, reinstall_withdrawals, reset_offer, standing, unresolved; refusal_reasons: barrier, binding, continuation; request_operations: delivery_reboot, exec; sources: adapter_read, job_record; start_members: associations, calls, current_installations, dispatched, dispositions, durable, prerequisite_records, reboot_results, reinstall_approvals, reinstall_withdrawals, reset_offer, standing, unresolved. Each pair below is a negative control: production matches the refused side and differs from the admitted side; commandHold: TauWeb.Dispatch.command_holds_delivery_reboot versus TauWeb.Dispatch.delivery_reboot_without_hold; rebootBootChange: TauWeb.Dispatch.delivery_reboot_same_boot_refused versus TauWeb.Dispatch.delivery_reboot_same_boot_admitted_without_guard; destructiveStops: TauWeb.Dispatch.destructive_choice_stops_delivery_reboot versus TauWeb.Dispatch.delivery_reboot_dispatched_without_destructive_stop. The record names the rule, file, bound, spec and implementation revisions. Make CNF-3's three breaks once by hand and record each red trace: flip an expected outcome in a scratch file, remove or empty the file, and introduce an unrecognised event kind or outcome. This split is an implementation reading of ADR-0032. The file's bound is covered only by the three runs together: witnesses by all three, enumerated traces by twr-ggw.8 and twr-i6k.3. The reboot bucket has zero enumerated traces because the alphabet has neither delivery_reboot nor collect_reboot; its 12 witnesses are its whole comparison. Dispatch witnesses omit ARC-43's pending-delivery-check hold and lifecycle reads; an exec after settled delivery_reboot represents one after the verdict. Those integrated cases need separate evidence [CNF-3, ADR-0032, STA-20, STA-24, ARC-43].

```python
def rescue(t):
    start=t['start']; dispositions=list(start['dispositions'])
    if start['reset_offer'] or any(start[k] for k in
            ('reinstall_approvals','reinstall_withdrawals','prerequisite_records')):
        return True
    for step in t['steps']:
        e=step['event']; kind=e['kind']
        if kind in ('reset_prereqs','approve_reinstall','withdraw_reinstall'):
            return True
        if kind in ('request','read'):
            if e['operation'] in ('activate','register_key'): return True
            if kind=='request' and e['operation']=='reset' and any(
                    d['continuation']=='destructive_reinstall' for d in dispositions):
                return True
        if kind=='dispose': dispositions.append(e)
    return False

def reboot(t):
    s=t['start']
    return bool(s.get('reboot_results')) or any(
        c['operation']=='delivery_reboot' for c in s['calls']) or any(
        x['event']['kind']=='collect_reboot' or (
            x['event']['kind']=='request' and x['event']['operation']=='delivery_reboot')
        for x in t['steps'])

def dispatch(t):
    if rescue(t): return 'dedicated'
    if reboot(t): return 'reboot'
    return 'stage1'
```

## Not this ticket's
LNVPS's typed restart, its survival evidence, settlement refusal and pending-delivery-check hold, and exec of the same reboot bytes stay in twr-ggw.36. The service boot anchor and running-at-delivery re-entry cases are twr-ggw.73's. This comparison is evidence about harness knowledge, never external state, effect ordering or concurrency.

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.8 — production dispatch comparator and shared admission core
- twr-ggw.69 — STA-20's unresolved-command hold and commandHold negative control
- twr-ggw.12 — durable tracked job records and collection
- twr-ggw.36 — composed service reads and delivery-check evidence

## Spec
ADR-0032, ADR-0050, ARC-43, CNF-110, CNF-3, CNF-40, CNF-53, CNF-55, STA-20, STA-24, STA-3

title: Robot typed operations over the pinned tunnel
description:
## What to build
Key registration, rescue activation and the resets run against a fixture Robot through the tunnel, reconcile-before-retry, and are confirmed only by STG-4's predicates. The activation's root password is redacted by twr-ggw.9's boundary before journal or model. A lost reset requested again under a fresh call id is refused, and so is an activation after an unresolved registration.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each Robot mutation is journaled before send, and killing the worker between record and send leaves the record [CNF-28 (Robot's)].
- [ ] Each is confirmed only by its STG-4 predicate, never by its own response or a clock [STG-4, STA-5].
- [ ] A lost reset followed by the model requesting it again under a new call id is refused [CNF-29 (Robot)].
- [ ] An activation after an unresolved key registration is refused [CNF-29, STG-4].
- [ ] The activation's root password is absent from the journal and model context [CNF-14 (rescue), SEC-5 row 9].

- [ ] Immediately before every reset into rescue, ordinary ceremony included, read the activation predicate and durably journal it. Dispatch only when that immediately preceding read confirms activation; nonconfirmation or failed append visibly refuses with no reset. For an approval-bound reset require activation dispatched since that approval. A matching old read cannot substitute for this read; test independently of the companion's coarser traces [STG-4, STG-20, CNF-38].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.72 — requirements at spec 8869ade
- twr-i6k.1 — The pinned tunnel: TLS to a vendor API inside the browser, over the relay
- twr-ggw.9 — One credential-redaction boundary before the journal and the model
- twr-ggw.11 — Binding: a session holds only its bound machine's key

## Spec
CHN-R1, STG-3a, STG-4, STA-5, STA-24, SEC-5 row 9, CNF-14, CNF-28, CNF-29, CNF-38, STG-20

comments.author: user
comments.text:
At spec ee133d0 (twr-ggw.60's pin), AC2's STG-4 confirmation predicates and AC4's
unresolved-registration refusal are unchanged. STG-4 adds a separate duty immediately before
the reset into rescue at which a standing disposition's destructive reinstall is dispatched:
read the activation predicate again and durably journal that read; only a re-read the journal
holds discharges it, and it does not extend to the ordinary install ceremony's reset into

title: The rescue ceremony: a host-key pin at both hops, rescue job records and the blocked append
description:
## What to build
The rescue system's host-key pin is read from the vendor after the reset, per boot, and nothing connects before it is published; the ready-to-reset job journals the installed system's host-key pins before the reset is offered, and a key the model emits never becomes a pin. Rescue jobs are never launched twice within a boot, and with the journal append blocked no reset is offered or dispatched; once the append is allowed, records and pins are recovered and dispatch resumes on the reset's confirmation. The dispatch core runs the companion comparison over the dedicated rescue-rule bucket; twr-i6k.11 owns the separate reboot bucket.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The rescue host-key pin is read from the vendor after the reset and before the first connection, and the activation response is never a host-key source [CNF-22, STG-4].
- [ ] The installed system's host-key pins come from the ready-to-reset job's own output, and a different key the model emits in its text is not pinned [CNF-22, ARC-43].
- [ ] CNF-38's four cases pass [CNF-38, STG-11].
- [ ] With SSH dropped during partitioning, the returning session reads the same rescue boot's job and does not duplicate it, including under a new command id [CNF-86, STA-20b].
- [ ] With the journal append blocked before the planned reboot, no reset is offered and none dispatched, including through a separately requested typed operation; once allowed, records and pins are recovered and dispatch resumes on the reset's confirmation, not on reconnection [CNF-86, STA-20b].
- [ ] An unexpected rescue reboot leaves the old command unresolved until the operator's disposition, continuing on what inspection shows or choosing a new destructive reinstall [CNF-86].
- [ ] With an unresolved Robot activation or key registration disposed under either continuation that continues, a box-plane command is dispatched: "a disposed create, activation or key registration bars nothing on the box plane"; this ticket exercises the activation and key-registration cases [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] With an unresolved Robot activation disposed toward a destructive reinstall or abandonment, the model's box-plane command to that machine is refused, "whatever the disposed call was" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] While a destructive-reinstall disposition stands, the rescue activation and a key registration where one is owed "are admitted and do not end the restriction"; the model's command refused before either is still refused after it [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] Under a standing destructive-reinstall disposition, a reset with no confirmed rescue activation is refused: "Any other reset is refused while the disposition stands"; the disposition and its restriction remain standing [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] After rescue activation confirmation, a reset whose newest journaled activation read reports it inactive is refused with the disposition still standing: "A read that does not confirm the activation, inactive or one that tells nothing, leaves it not counted"; the activation call stays terminal [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] At reinstall continuation dispatch count only an activation dispatched since the standing disposition and still confirmed by its newest durable predicate read. Reject predecessor/replaced-choice activations. Exercise a new activation while armed and record the vendor's actual answer independently of its confirming predicate; admit a confirming re-read reset and end the restriction at intent [STA-24, STG-4, CNF-110].
- [ ] Evidence appended after a disposition "neither reopens the call nor removes the disposition"; a read of the rescue activation decides which reset counts, using the newest journaled activation-predicate read before the reset's intent, never `/rescue/last`, and "reopens nothing and removes nothing" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] The host-pin core passes the companion comparison over the pins witness traces twr-ggw.43 left to this ticket, the twr-i6k.3 bucket of pins-witnesses-v5.json, schema 5: 21 witnesses and 4090 enumerated traces at `8869ade`. This ticket must pass step 1's rescue traces holding reset or rescue_last and no attest, and step 4's traces: a new job-read pin admission or a job-read attempt after a published pin, with no rescue step, including ready_to_reset, reinstall, connect. The pinned applicability table in 07-conformance.md assigns these cases: "Its new job-read pin admission, initial-group opening by a job read, and job-read attempt after a published pin belong to the dedicated row". Use this single decision list, written so it can be pasted into the test, first match wins. Step 1: a trace holding reset or rescue_last goes to the attest row if it also holds attest, otherwise to twr-i6k.3. Step 2: otherwise send it to twr-ggw.43 if it holds neither attest nor ready_to_reset, or if all attest/ready_to_reset steps are a pinned leading prefix followed by a published step. Step 3: otherwise send a trace holding attest to the attest row. Step 4: otherwise send it to twr-i6k.3. Read start records before the first step. Unknown schema, event kind, outcome or projection member fails naming the trace. Compare every owned outcome and knowledge projection at every step; each refused/admitted pair stays whole. At 8869ade the buckets sum to 75 witnesses and 8421 enumerated traces, bound 3 over 20: twr-ggw.43 has 39 / 2185, twr-i6k.3 has 21 / 4090, and the outstanding attest row has 15 / 2146. The file's bound is covered only by twr-ggw.43's and twr-i6k.3's runs together with the attest row's run, which is outstanding; deferral enables nothing. All 832 enumerated rescue-plus-attest traces (no named witnesses hold both) go to attest, with every step left to that run. The record names the rule, file, bound, spec and implementation revisions. CNF-3's three breaks each turn this comparison red, naming the trace, made once by hand and recorded here: flip an expected outcome in a scratch file; remove or empty the file; supply an unrecognised event kind or outcome [CNF-3, CNF-84, CNF-109, ADR-0032].

```python
def pins(trace):
    steps=trace['steps']; kinds={s['event']['kind'] for s in steps}
    if kinds & {'reset','rescue_last'}:
        return 'attest' if 'attest' in kinds else 'dedicated'
    sources=[n for n,s in enumerate(steps) if s['event']['kind'] in ('attest','ready_to_reset')]
    if not sources: return 'stage1'
    if sources==list(range(len(sources))) and all(steps[n]['pinned'] for n in sources) and any(
        s['event']['kind']=='published' for s in steps[len(sources):]):
        return 'stage1'
    if 'attest' in kinds: return 'attest'
    return 'dedicated'
```

The three buckets sum to 97 witnesses and 470 enumerated traces. Bound: 3 events over an alphabet of 8, filtered to distinct request call ids. Use the single step test below in all three comparisons: rescue first, then reboot content in start or steps, then stage1. Presence of empty reboot_results or nonempty current_installations alone never routes a trace. Every refused/admitted pair stays whole. Unknown schema, kind, operation, continuation, source, outcome or projection member fails naming the trace. Compare every outcome and projection at every step, starting with the start records. Measured vocabulary: continuations: abandonment, as_if_done, as_if_not_done, destructive_reinstall; kinds: approve_reinstall, dispose, read, replay, request, reset_prereqs, withdraw_reinstall; operations: activate, exec, register_key, reinstall, reset; outcome_members: dispatch, disposition, offer, refusal, settled, withdrawal; projection_members: associations, calls, current_installations, dispatched, dispositions, durable, prerequisite_records, reboot_results, reinstall_approvals, reinstall_withdrawals, reset_offer, standing, unresolved; refusal_reasons: approval_activation, barrier, binding, continuation, withdrawn_approval; request_operations: activate, exec, register_key, reinstall, reset; sources: adapter_read, job_record, pin_checked_handshake; start_members: associations, calls, current_installations, dispatched, dispositions, durable, prerequisite_records, reboot_results, reinstall_approvals, reinstall_withdrawals, reset_offer, standing, unresolved. Each pair below is a negative control: production matches the refused side and differs from the admitted side; approvalResetRequiresRescue: TauWeb.Dispatch.approval_reset_requires_rescue_refused versus TauWeb.Dispatch.approval_reset_requires_rescue_admitted_without_guard; resetOfferFreshKeys: TauWeb.Dispatch.kept_keys_reset_offer_refused versus TauWeb.Dispatch.kept_keys_reset_offer_admitted_without_guard; reinstallWithdrawalEffective: TauWeb.Dispatch.withdrawn_approval_reset_refused versus TauWeb.Dispatch.withdrawn_approval_reset_admitted_without_guard; approvedReinstallBoundary: TauWeb.Dispatch.approved_reinstall_boundary_refused versus TauWeb.Dispatch.approved_reinstall_boundary_admitted_without_guard; failedPrerequisiteWithdraws: TauWeb.Dispatch.failed_prerequisite_withdrawal_refused versus TauWeb.Dispatch.failed_prerequisite_withdrawal_admitted_without_guard; resetOfferCurrentInstallation: TauWeb.Dispatch.predecessor_reset_offer_refused versus TauWeb.Dispatch.predecessor_reset_offer_admitted_without_guard; resetOfferCurrentInstallation: TauWeb.Dispatch.changed_keys_reset_offer_refused versus TauWeb.Dispatch.changed_keys_reset_offer_admitted_without_guard; durableBeforeApply: TauWeb.Dispatch.reset_offered_after_failed_append_refused versus TauWeb.Dispatch.reset_offered_after_failed_append_admitted; reach: TauWeb.Dispatch.continuing_permits_what_was_barred versus TauWeb.Dispatch.disposed_activation_bars_commands_without_guard; resetIntoRescueOnly: TauWeb.Dispatch.reset_without_rescue_refused versus TauWeb.Dispatch.reset_without_rescue_admitted; newestActivationRead: TauWeb.Dispatch.spent_activation_not_counted versus TauWeb.Dispatch.spent_activation_counted_without_guard; lapse: TauWeb.Dispatch.preparation_keeps_restriction versus TauWeb.Dispatch.preparation_lifts_restriction_without_guard. The record names the rule, file, bound, spec and implementation revisions. Make CNF-3's three breaks once by hand and record each red trace: flip an expected outcome in a scratch file, remove or empty the file, and introduce an unrecognised event kind or outcome. This split is an implementation reading of ADR-0032. The file's bound is covered only by the three runs together: witnesses by all three, enumerated traces by twr-ggw.8 and twr-i6k.3. The reboot bucket has zero enumerated traces because the alphabet has neither delivery_reboot nor collect_reboot; its 12 witnesses are its whole comparison. Dispatch witnesses omit ARC-43's pending-delivery-check hold and lifecycle reads; an exec after settled delivery_reboot represents one after the verdict. Those integrated cases need separate evidence [CNF-3, ADR-0032, STA-20, STA-24, ARC-43].

```python
def rescue(t):
    start=t['start']; dispositions=list(start['dispositions'])
    if start['reset_offer'] or any(start[k] for k in
            ('reinstall_approvals','reinstall_withdrawals','prerequisite_records')):
        return True
    for step in t['steps']:
        e=step['event']; kind=e['kind']
        if kind in ('reset_prereqs','approve_reinstall','withdraw_reinstall'):
            return True
        if kind in ('request','read'):
            if e['operation'] in ('activate','register_key'): return True
            if kind=='request' and e['operation']=='reset' and any(
                    d['continuation']=='destructive_reinstall' for d in dispositions):
                return True
        if kind=='dispose': dispositions.append(e)
    return False

def reboot(t):
    s=t['start']
    return bool(s.get('reboot_results')) or any(
        c['operation']=='delivery_reboot' for c in s['calls']) or any(
        x['event']['kind']=='collect_reboot' or (
            x['event']['kind']=='request' and x['event']['operation']=='delivery_reboot')
        for x in t['steps'])

def dispatch(t):
    if rescue(t): return 'dedicated'
    if reboot(t): return 'reboot'
    return 'stage1'
```

- [ ] Immediately before every reset into rescue, ordinary ceremony included, read the activation predicate and durably journal it. Dispatch only when that immediately preceding read confirms activation; nonconfirmation or failed append visibly refuses with no reset. For an approval-bound reset require activation dispatched since that approval. A matching old read cannot substitute for this read; test independently of the companion's coarser traces [STG-4, STG-20, CNF-38].

- [ ] Continuing as if not done keeps the matching labelled root and its installed keys. Withhold reset on changed newest keys, absent durable result (including a failed read after an earlier successful one, across replay), predecessor prerequisites, or first-read overlap with earlier prerequisites/installed pins. Keep that first-read anchor even after a later disjoint read; show why before reboot. Derive installation at dispatch, and compare partial overlap against earlier observations in the pin backstop [STA-20b, STG-20, CNF-86].

- [ ] The rescue wait is STA-20's unresolved-command hold: collect rather than reissue; before a planned reset every tracked command needs a terminal record, not merely proven end. Dispose A to continue, dispatch B, then replace A's disposition with destructive reinstall: return to rescue waits for B and its collection, never for disposed A's record. Exercise the six enumerated box-plane requests refused behind unresolved commands; the existing blockers transitively reach twr-ggw.69 through twr-i6k.10 and twr-ggw.14 [STA-20, STA-20b, STA-24, CNF-86, ADR-0032].

description:
## What to build
The fetch_artifact job uses the immutable pinned URL and halts on a mismatch even when the model reports the right hash; Alpine's repository branch and accepted keys are enforced; and disk selection passes CNF-85 without writes. Both layers of artifact admission are recorded. When the installed system stays silent past its named wait, probed only by pinned SSH attempts, the install is declared failed and a separately approved reinstall is offered with the disks shown.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A mismatching artifact halts the install, also when the model reports the correct hash, and the machine does not continue unpinned [CNF-24, CNF-93 (halt), STG-6].
- [ ] The pinned URL is an immutable versioned path [CNF-66].
- [ ] Alpine checks the bundle's branch and accepted key set and records index digests and installed versions; an unsigned package, or one signed by an unaccepted key, is refused; and the build checks the declared key list against the pinned minirootfs's keyring [CNF-67 (Alpine), ARC-25a].

- [ ] Both layers of artifact admission are recorded, and the display distinguishes the bootstrap hash from package signatures [STG-6, CNF-67].
- [ ] An installed system that does not answer within the named wait is declared failed and the operator told; a missing bootloader and a relay outage each clear no unresolved operation and trigger no wipe without the operator's decision [CNF-80, STG-20].

title: Replace confirms the dedicated root relabel before removing the old key
description:
## What to build
Implement STA-17's dedicated-machine replace_root_label job in the one-machine Replace flow. The dedicated applicability row owns every CNF-20 relabel case, including its non-dedicated fixture; stage 1's LNVPS Replace writes no label.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After new-key connection confirmation and before old-key removal, issue a typed harness-composed replace_root_label on dedicated machines, selected from journal vendor records, never disk labels. Record before transmission, keep its machine-side job record, and refuse model requests [STA-17, ARC-7, ARC-8, ARC-43, STA-20, SEC-1, CNF-20].
- [ ] Write the new hexadecimal machine component with unchanged decimal ordinal. Confirm with a harness-composed label read after the write using captured job output. Move the shown id and remove the old key only once that read shows it [STA-17, STG-20, CNF-20].
- [ ] Failed write, wrong read-back or lost read-back keeps machine not migrated, old key and shown id unchanged, and Replace incomplete with machine/reason. Re-read on every later connection once STA-20 and STA-24 admit it, until confirmation; a matching read completes without rewriting. Any reissue is a fresh operator choice, never automatic [STA-17, STA-6, CNF-20].
- [ ] Exercise CNF-20 (a)-(f), including missing/damaged/foreign label on a dedicated machine and a non-dedicated fixture sending no job/writing no disk. Reject unfinished rescue installs even after pins until installed reset confirmation, with visible machine/reason [STA-17, CNF-20, CNF-86].
- [ ] Re-enter rescue after confirmed migration: same ordinal, root matches shown new id and is kept/resumed. A failed write leaving label unchanged also keeps old id matching it. This tests the brief's use separately from the job's read-back [CNF-86, STG-20].

- [ ] Under each of destructive reinstall and abandonment, refuse replace_root_label and its label re-read before dispatch, whoever starts it and whatever call was disposed. Status queries admitted by STA-24, pinned SSH attempts and record collection remain permitted and end no restriction; a harness-composed box-plane read is a command [STA-24, CNF-110, ADR-0050].

- [ ] Exercise CNF-40's held-harness-job case for replace_root_label and its label re-read: STA-20's unresolved-command hold records no intent and queues no job; the visible flow composes a first issue afresh after release, once under one intent. Stopping its wait leaves nothing armed through replay; only an operator act resumes that stopped flow [STA-20, CNF-40].

- [ ] On a dedicated machine under STA-20's unresolved-command hold or a standing destructive reinstall or abandonment disposition, compose no replace_root_label. After admission returns, the relabel is a first issue after the key install and new-key connection confirmation, before old-key removal, in STA-17's order. twr-ggw.29 owns the Replace-wide not-yet-migrated display and completion rule [STA-17, STA-20, STA-24, CNF-20].
